q.en: You are a project manager in an IT project. During the deployment of a new system, an unexpected power outage occurs. What should the project manager do?

en: Perform a qualitative risk analysis
Refer to the risk register and inform key stakeholders
Risk probability and impact assessment
Risk categorization

x.en: As an unexpected power outage occurs, the project manager should first Refer to the risk register and inform key stakeholders to handle this scenario. Risk categorization and Risk probability and impact assessment are T&T in Perform a qualitative risk analysis process, therefore they can be excluded.

q.en: Which of the following Processes must the project manager perform to avoid scope creep caused by uncontrolled changes?

en: Perform Qualitative Risk Analysis Process
Perform integrated change control process
Validate Scope Process
Control Quality Process

x.en: The uncontrolled expansion to product or project scope without adjustments to time, cost, and resources is referred to as scope creep. Change is inevitable, so the project manager must perform all changes through the Integrated Change Control process to avoid scope creep caused by uncontrolled changes.

q.en: During a project, a project manager realizes that a new stakeholder is interested in the project and wants to ensure the stakeholder is fully aware of the goals, objectives, and risks of the project. As a project manager, what should you do to enhance the success of the project?

en: Add the new stakeholder to the communications management plan
Schedule a meeting with the new stakeholder
Update the stakeholder engagement plan
Share the project status reports with the new stakeholder

x.en: Keyword ( a project manager realizes) so the project manager already classified the stakeholders that he is an interested stakeholder. so the next step is to Update the stakeholder engagement plan based on his needs, expectations, interests, and potential impact on the project to enhance the success of the project.

q.en: A project manager has been assigned to a new digital product line, which the company hopes will boost their revenue. The product is complex and requires customer feedback to continually refine the product The project is being handled by across-functional agile team. What should the project manager do to ensure value is delivered quickly?

en: Identify tasks that can run in parallel to deliver the project faster
Request a budget increase to pay the subject matter experts (SMEs) moreover time
Ask the project sponsor to provide additional resources to fast-track the project.
Plan the project to deliver value incrementally with regular releases

x.en:
One means of delivering value sooner rather than later is via incremental delivery. Early and regular incremental releases lead to higher customer value and an increased market share.
Dividing the product into increments enables parts or elements of the product to be in the hands of customers prior to full delivery of the product.

q.en: A major issue about conflicting priorities has been highlighted by the project team with regard to a few stakeholder requirements. What should the project manager do?

en: Allow the project team to decide what is the most appropriate requirement to follow.
Escalate to the project management office(PMO) and request a solution for the requirements
Negotiate a common agreement with the involved stakeholders regarding the requirements
Prioritize other items for the team and deal with the conflicting requirements later

x.en: Keyword (conflicting priorities) so the project manager should use negotiation skills so the correct answer " Negotiate a common agreement with the involved stakeholders regarding the requirements".

q.en: A project manager is reviewing the lessons learned for a historical project. The review identifies that the client's engineer was adamant that they review all changes, even those not identified in the contract. How should the project manager deal with this when planning the project?

en: Update the project risk register to identify this risk and describe how to mitigate the issue
Ensure the change management plan highlights this requirement to prevent future issues
Update the project charter with this information regarding change management
Talk with the client to ensure they are aware of the change management procedure

x.en: The review identifies that the client's engineer was adamant that they review all changes so the project manager should Ensure the change management plan highlights this requirement to prevent future issues.

q.en: A project team needs to follow regulatory compliance guidelines that are mandatory for the project. What should the project manager do to ensure compliance adherence?

en: Assess compliance when there is time in the project
Include compliance within the development tools
Assign a project team member to ensure compliance
Review compliance adherence at the end of the project.

x.en: A project team needs to follow regulatory compliance guidelines that are mandatory for the project so the project manager should Assign a project team member to ensure compliance

q.en: A complex project is in the execution phase. A key stakeholder who is new to the project has not been approving project deliverables, which could impact the overall progress. What should the project manager do next?

en: Meet with the stakeholder to understand what is causing the delays.
Facilitate a brainstorming session to find potential workarounds
Capture this in the issue log and escalate it to the project sponsor.
Discuss the need to influence this stakeholder with the sponsor.

x.en: Keyword (not been approving project deliverables -impact the overall progress) so the project manager should meet with the stakeholder to understand what is causing the delays.

q.en: An organization imports many of the materials for a product build. Due to global shipping delays, some of the essential materials have yet to arrive. resulting in the inability to finish building the product for the upcoming release. The project manager is meeting with stakeholders to discuss options. What should the project manager recommend?

en: Request marketing to launch an advertising campaign for the product that IS currently in stock
Explore if the materials could be supplied locally and obtained on time.
Meet with the engineering team to manufacture the materials in-house
Update the project management plan, factoring in furloughs of the assembly team to reduce expenses

x.en: Due to the inability to finish building the product for the upcoming release, the project manager should Explore if the materials could be supplied locally and obtained on time.

q.en: Two teams are engaged in a global project. After the first release, many issues were identified on the product, which could easily have been avoided with better communication. What should the project manager do?

en: Facilitate a meeting with both teams so that they can agree on the issues and propose solutions that work for both teams
Improve the videoconferencing system to provide better availability and quality in order to increase communication
Have team ambassadors from each location travel to the other in order to facilitate communication and minimize issues
Improve the Email system to provide better availability and quality in order to increase communication

x.en:
An interactive model of communication is the best communication method to solve problems.
The project manager should facilitate a meeting with both teams so that they can agree on the issues and propose solutions that work for both teams

q.en: A new development project is about to start, and the project manager knows that a high-proof customer makes very specific and frequent requests in all sprints. This project will demand contract coordination with third parties, and the project manager must find a better way to manage customer and partner expectations. What strategy should the project manager use?

en: Work very closely with the customer and third parties to meet their needs
Specify the scope and features to be deployed in the contract clearly
Focus on the implementation of software as a service solution for the customer
Change the marketing and product management definitions to meet stakeholder needs

x.en: The best way to manage customer and partner expectations "Work very closely with the customer and third parties to meet their needs"

q.en: A project's business case was just approved and the project manager is creating the benefits management plan. It is unclear how the benefits from the project align with the organization's vision. What should the project manager do first to verify alignment?

en: Meet with the project sponsor to obtain more information.
Ask the project team to delay the kick-off while resolving the concern
Request a copy of the project assumptions log for more insight
Consult with the project team members to gain their opinions

x.en: To verify alignment with the organization's vision, the project manager should Meet with the project sponsor to obtain more information.

q.en: A company has undertaken a large transformation project in preparation for the changing economy. During the planning of the transformation project, the key resource from human resources (HR) refuses to approve the proposed project plan. What should the project manager do to gain an understanding of the cause for the resource's refusal?

en: Speak with their colleague.
Communicate with their supervisor.
Speak directly with the resource
Organize a team meeting

x.en: As a project manager, you should Speak directly with the resource to understand why he refuses to approve the proposed project plan.

q.en: The ____________ is also called "the voice of the customer"?

en: Product Owner
Scrum Master
Development team
Sponsor

x.en: Because the Product Owner must understand the needs and priorities of the stakeholders, including customers and users, this role is commonly referred to as the Voice of the Customer. It is the needs and priorities of stakeholders that demand flexibility in applying Scrum.

q.en: A stakeholder requests John the Scrum Master, to show him the latest weekly status report to check the project's health and the remaining amount of work in the project. Instead, John takes the stakeholder to the team wall where a few pertinent updates are posted continuously. To address the stakeholder's query, John specifically points out to

en: Velocity trend
Sprint backlog
Burndown chart
Kanban board

x.en: A burndown chart shows the amount of work that has been completed in a sprint, and the total work remaining.

q.en: One developer's productivity is lacking compared with the others due to repetitive attendance issues. What should the project manager do to determine the appropriate disciplinary actions specific to this project?

en: Review RACI chart
Review the Stakeholder register
Review the organizational process assets
Check the resource management plan

x.en: The resource management plan provides guidance on various aspects of team development including disciplinary actions as a result of team performance assessments.

q.en: An agile project is running its fifth iteration out of eight. A stakeholder is not happy with the progress the team made so far. The stakeholder approaches the team and requests that from now on the team informs her about the status of their work on an ongoing basis. How should a servant leader respond?

en: Suggest that the stakeholder periodically reviews the information radiators.
Invite the stakeholder to the daily standups, iteration reviews, and retrospectives
Provide the stakeholder with the performance measurement baseline.
Explain to the stakeholder that agile projects discourage progress monitoring

x.en: An information radiator is a visible, physical (or electronic) display that provides project information to the stakeholders enabling up-to-the-minute knowledge sharing without having to disturb the project team. In the reference provided, one of the Agile Manifesto authors, says that an information radiator "displays information in a place where passersby can see it. With information radiators, the passerby does not need to ask questions; the information simply hits them as they pass by." In the scenario provided, an information radiator, such as a Kanban board and/or a burndown chart, can allow the stakeholder to monitor the progress of the user stories being developed by the team. Kanban board can display work in progress at each stage of development. A burndown chart allows seeing how much work remained to be completed in a release or an iteration. Of the choices provided, suggesting that the stakeholder periodically reviews the information radiators would address the stakeholder's request to monitor the status of the team's work on an ongoing basis and is, therefore, the best answer to the question asked.

q.en: During the demo of an agile project. the client states that the product does not reflect the product vision and requirements initially discussed. The client says that the product needs significant changes before it would be acceptable. What might have prevented this situation?

en: Following a more rigorous organization's change control process
Managing conflicts more efficiently between the client and the team
Isolating the development team from stakeholders to avoid distraction
Allowing higher transparency of the work in front of the stakeholders

x.en: To accelerate the sharing of information among stakeholders, agile methods promote aggressive transparency. For example, agile encourages inviting any stakeholders (which would include the client) to project meetings and reviews to surface as quickly as possible any misalignment, dependency, or other issue related to the changing project. Also, many agile teams post information radiators (project status and progress artifacts) in public spaces for everybody to view.

q.en: What is the ScrumMaster responsible for?

en: The Development Team's meetings and for the objectives the Development Team outlines for itself.
Defining the Development Team's tasks during the Sprint.
Imposing metrics and managing the performance of the Development Team.
Teaching Scrum and seeing that it is adopted and used correctly.

x.en: The scrum master is responsible for ensuring the Scrum process is upheld and works to ensure the Scrum team adheres to the practices and rules as well as coaches the team on removing impediments. PMI Practice guide page, 101

q.en: A project manager notices that there is limited participation and contribution from a new team member. What should the project manager do?

en: Write a complaint to the human resources department.
Review the roles and responsibilities of each team member.
Discuss the situation with the project sponsor.
Discipline the new team member.

x.en:
Very important question in real exam 

The Project manager should FIRST (Discipline - Correction - Direction ) the new team member because of his limited participation and contribution.

q.en: During regular team meetings, the project manager notices that there are clear signs of conflict and issues related to unclear task assignments and ownership. What should the project manager do to address this?

en: Meet individually with team members to understand the conflicts and issues.
Investigate possible ways to improve team collaboration and morale.
Change the structure of the regular project meetings to improve communication.
Define and obtain agreement on a responsible accountable, consult, and inform RACI Matrix.

x.en: Keyword (unclear task assignments and ownership ). A RACI Matrix is a useful tool to use to ensure clear assignment of roles and responsibilities when the team consists of internal and external resources. So the project manager should Define and obtain agreement on a responsible accountable, consult, and inform RACI Matrix to adress this situation.

q.en: One month into a 12-month project., a vendor informs the project manager that required project equipment will be delayed. After further investigation, the project manager learns that this vendor has a reputation for underperforming. What should the project manager have done to prevent this?

en: Reviewed the lessons learned documents from other projects
Check the updated risk register and issue log
Included a contingency buffer in the schedule baseline
Added a backup vendor to the vendor list

x.en: To prevent this situation, the project manager should have reviewed the lessons learned documents from other projects to know more about the reputation of vendor.

q.en: Your software development project is in initiation. The sponsor wants to take advantage of early revenue from incremental delivery and pushes to use an agile approach. However, the team is strongly opposed to agile due to strife among the team members. They insist on a predictive approach so they can work independently with individual task assignments. What is your best course of action to address these conflicts?

en: Select a predictive approach to avoid conflict among the team members
Adopt an XP framework since it is agile, but team members work independently
Apply an agile project management approach as requested by the sponsor
Recommend to lead the project using a hybrid project management approach

x.en:
Very important question in real exam 

A hybrid approach would provide the opportunity for early revenue generation through incremental delivery as requested by the sponsor while allowing the project team members to work independently with individually assigned tasks.

q.en: As a scrum master, you are facilitating a retrospective for a sprint that failed to meet all of its objectives. Members of the development team and the product owner are arguing over who is responsible for the failure. After performing a root cause analysis, you uncover the source of the conflict. Of the following, what did you most likely discover?

en: The Gantt chart did not include enough story points.
You, as the scrum master, failed to assign user stories to the development team.
The product owner determined how many user stories were to be completed during the sprint.
The development team decided how many user stories were to be completed during the sprint.

x.en: When properly using a scrum framework, the product owner prioritizes the user stories in the product backlog. The product owner, however, should not determine 'how many' user stories will be completed during the sprint. Instead, it is the development team members who decide how many user stories they can commit to completing. If the product owner overcommitted the development team, then the sprint will likely fail to meet some or all of its objectives. Additionally, if the product owner assigns the work to the development team, then the team is less likely to be fully committed to completing the sprint objectives. The incorrect answer choices represent the correct application of scrum best practices or are not relevant to scrum.

q.en: As part of the Estimate Activity Durations process, the project manager facilitates a sprint planning meeting with the product owner and Scrum team. The project manager breaks down the user stories into low-level tasks, estimates the time required in hours, and determines the sprint backlog based on the team's capacity. Despite meticulous planning, the sprint fails. What might the project manager have done differently?

en: Used story points instead of hours while estimating the size of the user stories and tasks
Empowered the team to determine how many user stories they can complete during the sprint
Asked the team to prioritize the product backlog before determining the sprint backlog
Assigned the identified low-level tasks to specific individuals in the project schedule

x.en: The scenario suggests a hybrid project management approach is used in the project by incorporating Scrum into a predictive model. In Scrum, the team is empowered to determine how many user stories they can complete during a sprint.

q.en: Which of the following are components of a Resource Calendar? (Choose two.)

en: Training Strategies
Recognition Plans
Working days
Availability of physical resource

x.en: A resource calendar identifies the working days, shifts, start and end of normal business hours, weekends, and public holidays when each specific resource is available. PMBOK 6th edition page, 323

q.en: A project manager working with the team to develop a software application. Due to failures in similar applications in the past, the rapid feedback from the customer on the suitability of the deliverables is very important. What is the best approach that should be selected?

en: Adaptive
Waterfall
Traditional
Predictive

x.en: An adaptive approach is a generic term for various project management approaches typically used on agile projects. This approach promotes the work to be undertaken in short cycles so that the results can be reviewed early and adapted as necessary. Of the choices provided, the adaptive approach is the only one that would provide rapid feedback on the suitability of the deliverables making this choice the best answer to the question

q.en: A project manager is assigned to a project in a company that is transitioning to agile. During the sprint retrospective meeting, the meeting becomes slightly contentious with the first signs of conflict between several team members. What is the best course of action for the project manager?

en: Address the situation during the meeting to hold the individuals who are involved in the conflict accountable
Intervene only if the conflict becomes destructive and take a break if needed to address individuals privately
Intervene immediately to avoid further escalation and damaged relationships between the team members
Do not intervene regardless of what happens since agile teams are self-managing and can handle anything

x.en: Conflict is inevitable and can be beneficial to a project when it promotes team discussion and encourages debate. It is important that the resolution of conflicts be encouraged, promoting an open environment where team members are empowered to express their opinions and concerns about the project. However, when conflict becomes destructive, it may be appropriate and necessary for the scrum master to intervene. The appropriate action for the scrum master to take in this circumstance would be to take a break and address individuals in private. In the scenario, however, the conflict is still at its very beginning. There is not enough information in the scenario to determine if the conflict is going to escalate and become destructive. Therefore, at this point, no action is needed from the scrum master. To select the correct answer in this particular question, one should compare the situation described in the scenario with the wording of the available choices. "Only if the conflict becomes destructive" is the key part that makes intervening only if the conflict becomes destructive and taking a break if needed to address individuals privately the best answer to the question asked.

q.en: You are a project manager for the internal project that will deliver a new tool to the performing organization for use by its employees. A conflict occurred between the project team and the training manager. The team wants to use short development cycles to gain early feedback and manage the high rate of change coming from the employees. The training manager, on the other hand, insists on creating a detailed training plan upfront to train the employees. What is the best way for the project manager to resolve the conflict?

en: Facilitate a compromise by adopting a hybrid approach
Avoid the conflict by escalating the issue to the project sponsor
Emphasize the commonalities between both approaches
Force an agile framework to satisfy the project team

x.en: Using an agile approach for product development and then a predictive approach for training should resolve the conflict. The hybrid approach is the logical choice based on the limited information provided in the scenario.

q.en: You are a project manager managing a large software project. Your project team sent confidential information to the subcontractor by mistake. What could have prevented this situation?

en: Review stakeholder register
Reviewing the Communication management Plan
Reviewing the Scope management Plan
Reviewing the stakeholder engagement Plan

x.en: The communications management plan is a component of the project management plan that describes how project communications will be planned, structured, implemented, and monitored for effectiveness. The plan contains the following information: Person responsible for authorizing the release of confidential information; Stakeholder communication requirements; Escalation processes; Timeframe and frequency for the distribution of required information and Person responsible for communicating the information.

q.en: Which of the following interpersonal and team skills helps to reduce misunderstandings and improves communication and knowledge sharing?

en: Leadership
Political awareness
Lessons learned register
Active listening

x.en: Active listening helps reduce misunderstandings and improves communication and knowledge sharing.

q.en: During a risk review meeting, the team identifies a risk. The project manager is unable to determine a way to manage the risk internally because it is in the domain of another project team. What should the project manager do?

en: Transfer the risk to another team
Accept the risk
Mitigate the risk
Escalate the risk to senior management.

x.en: Keyword( The risk in the domain of another project team) Escalation is appropriate when the project team or the project sponsor agrees that a threat is outside the scope of the project or that the proposed response would exceed the project manager's authority. Escalated risks are managed at the program level, portfolio level, or other relevant part of the organization, and not on the project level. The project manager determines who should be notified about the threat and communicates the details to that person or part of the organization. It is important that ownership of escalated threats is accepted by the relevant party in the organization.

q.en: Conformance to requirements and fitness for use are key concepts in quality management. Which of the following is another name for customer needs?

en: Voice of the Customer
Prompt list
Scope creep
Process mapping

x.en: In quality management, customer needs and requirements are also known as voice of the customer (VOC). [PMBOK® Guide 6th edition, Page 145]

q.en: Although people may say they can identify, assess, and manage their personal feelings, many teams experience tension and uncooperative behaviors among teammates. You have recognized this on projects where you have been a team member, especially virtual teams. Now that you are a professional project manager, you want to establish an environment in which teammates can reduce tension and increase cooperation. Which of the following is the best practice to follow?

en: Focus on goals to be served and ask that emotions be left outside the project
Use emotional intelligence to control the sentiments of team members
Maintain a good relationship with the project sponsor
Emphasize areas of agreement rather than areas of difference

x.en:
Very Important question in Real Exam 

Emotional intelligence (the ability to manage your emotions and others' emotions) leads directly to reducing conflict and making positive decisions.

q.en: As per the burn up chart shown below, what happened at day 7?

en: The team velocity increased
The team velocity decreased
Work was added to the scope
Work was removed from the scope

x.en:
At day 7, 2 points were removed from the scope, bringing the total in the backlog to 30 points so The right option is that work was removed from the scope.

But if in another scenario in real exam what is happend in 4 or 5 or 6 day the correct answer the scope has been increased.

q.en: As the project manager for a multinational company, you are responsible for new product development and maintenance of existing products. 90% of the development is outsourced to contract professionals. A system of processes is in place to consistently manage product development, and several contracts are used to control the work and ensure acceptable work is performed. After a contractor reports completion of a phase and the transfer of the completed deliverable's to others, what is your next step?

en: Pay invoices
Update the training certifications
Review customer acceptance documentation
Audit payment records

x.en: After a contractor reports completion of a phase and the transfer of the completed deliverables to others, your next step is to review customer acceptance documentation from the Validate Scope process.

q.en: You are attending a project status update meeting at the organization level. All attendees receive a dashboard of cost metrics of each project, and each project manager is presenting the status of his project. The metrics of one project shows a BAC of $120,000, AC of $99,000 and an EAC of $125,000. However, the project manager states that the ETC will be $20,000. What should you do?

en: Notify the senior management that there is a calculation error
Do nothing
Congratulate the project manager for being under budget
Advise the project manager to use fund from the contingency reserves of the project

x.en: As the ETC is being calculated and reported, that means the EAC= AC+ETC, so there is calculation error. As per the PMI code of ethics, you should report any mistake you observe to the appropriate management.

q.en: You are the project manager for a software project. As you are defining the scope of the work you need to do, you sit down with all of the project's stakeholders and record all of the requirements you can get from them. Which of the following is not a valid requirement from stakeholders?

en: There can be no more than 5% schedule variance on the project
The quality of the product must fit within organizational metrics for software quality
The work the team does must be better than they did on their last project
The budget must be within 10% of our projected cost

x.en: Saying that the work must be better is subjective. Requirements gathered in stakeholder analysis need to be quantifiable. That way, the team has a goal they can shoot for and you can always tell how close or far from it you are.

q.en: You are working for an automobile company, and you had conducted an independent estimate to find out the cost of sub-contracting the manufacturing of 1,000,000 ball bearings. You estimated the cost to be $800 per bearing. However, when you asked for bids and proposals from perspective sellers, the minimum price quoted was $1000 per bearing. Which of the following is not a reason for the variance in the estimate?

en: The procurement statement of work was not clear
There have not been major changes in cost of material and labor since the last year
The procurement statement of work was not sufficient
The perspective seller misunderstood the procurement statement of work

x.en: Significant differences in cost estimate can be an indication that the procurement statement of work was deficient, ambiguous, and/or that the perspective sellers either misunderstood or failed to respond fully to the procurement statement of work.

q.en:
During the last sprint review, the product owner stated that the product does not deliver any value. The project manager believes that the product meets all the provided specifications. The team is confused by the product owner's statement.
What should the project manager do when using a hybrid approach?

en: Prioritize the project backlog and ask the development team to x the issues
Review the project's benefits management plan with the product owner
Escalate the matter to the executive board so they can decide on next steps
Ask the product owner to terminate the project as it is no longer aligned to the expected benefits

x.en:
•The benefits management plan describes key elements of the benefits and may include but is not limited to: 

•Target benefits (financial value)
•Strategic alignment (e.g., how well the project benefits align to the business strategies of the organization) 

•Timeframe for realizing benefits (e.g., benefits by phase, short-term, long-term, and ongoing)
•Benefits owner (e.g., the accountable person to monitor, record, and report realized benefits)
•Metrics (e.g., the measures to be used to show benefits realized, direct measures, and indirect measures) •Risks (e.g., risks for realization of benefits).

q.en: A town wants to build a community center and has appointed a project manager. A site was found, and all of the necessary approvals and governance were completed. When the project kick-off was held, it was discovered that a local farmers' group was not consulted, and they use the site for a monthly market. What should the project manager do to move forward with the project?

en: Request that the project sponsor discuss compensation with the farmers' group for the lost business.
Document a risk related to the impact that the farmers' group could bring to the project.
Continue building the center as the farmers' group does not need to be consulted.
Discuss the project objectives with all stakeholders, including the farmers' group, and review their requirements.

x.en: Building a community center. After assigning the project manager the next step identify stakeholder and the local farmers are stakeholders and In the question scenario, it was mentioned that they were not consulted, so as a project manager should Discuss the project objectives with all stakeholders, including the farmers' group, and review their requirements.

q.en: A project manager prepared a project benefits management plan. Which of the following should be included in this document?

en: Strategic alignment, benefits owner, risk register
Target benefits, strategic alignment, time frame for realizing benefits
Project requirements, target benefits, issue log, metrics
Target benefits, benefits owner, lessons learned

x.en:
•The benefits management plan describes key elements of the benefits and may include but is not limited to: 

•Target benefits (financial value)
•Strategic alignment (e.g., how well the project benefits align to the business strategies of the organization) 

•Timeframe for realizing benefits (e.g., benefits by phase, short-term, long-term, and ongoing)
•Benefits owner (e.g., the accountable person to monitor, record, and report realized benefits)
•Metrics (e.g., the measures to be used to show benefits realized, direct measures, and indirect measures) •Risks (e.g., risks for realization of benefits).

q.en: A steering committee member is complaining about the weekly report. They stated that the report is too long and has unnecessary details. As a result, they are unable to obtain the main message and take action. What should the project manager do to avoid similar complaints?

en: Demonstrate the weekly reports in a presentation for the steering committee member.
Verify the information needed for steering committee members.
Send a shorter daily report to this steering committee member.
Present the status at a weekly meeting with the steering committee.

x.en: A steering committee member is complaining about the weekly report which is too long and has unnecessary details so the project manager should Verify the information needed for steering committee members to avoid similar complaints.

q.en: A few developers have identified a list of impediments at the daily standup and are asking for the project lead's assistance in prioritizing them. There are a few complex backlog items, and a new junior tester has identified a few compliance defects. The product owner and a couple of developers will be leaving the project team, and the contract with the test and production support partner will not be renewed. Which issue should the project lead focus on first?

en: Recruiting, on boarding, and training new developers.
Finding a new product owner to prioritize the product backlog.
Regulatory compliance issues discussed in the meeting.
Developing a new contract for production support.

x.en: The key word in the question is the product owner will leave the business, and there is complexity in the product backlog, so we are looking for the answer. Searching for a new product owner and priorities. My professional brother and sister notice that the international exam can be passed easily if you understand the scenarios of the question and look for the connection between the question and the answer.

q.en: During the execution of a construction project, one of the neighboring businesses is complaining that the current building height does not agree with the initial project plans. What should the project manager do first?

en: Ask the neighbor to leave the site immediately because the site is on private property.
Inform the neighbor that all of the project documentation has been approved.
Ask the neighbor to submit a formal complaint about their concerns.
Inform the neighbor that the complaint will be escalated to the project sponsor.

x.en: One of the neighboring businesses is complaining that the current building height does not agree with the initial project plans So the project manager should first Ask the neighbor to submit a formal complaint about their concerns.

q.en: A project manager is using an agile approach. During the sprint planning meeting, the product owner flagged a backlog item as high business value and easy to implement. However, the other team members identified a high dependency between this item and another item that is flagged as low business value and high complexity. What should the project manager do to support the backlog prioritization?

en: Prioritize the item flagged as high business value and low complexity for this sprint.
Facilitate the discussion until the team reaches an agreement about the two items.
Support the team to move both items to the next sprint when the team will know more.
Prioritize the item flagged as a dependency with low business value and high complexity.

x.en: There are different opinions with the team so project manager as servant leader should Facilitate the discussion until the team reaches an agreement about the two items.

q.en: An organization is using a hybrid delivery approach for a business project. The product owner, the person who was also managing the project, was promoted to a more senior role. A new project lead has joined the project. Which artifact should the project lead use to ensure that the project benefits have been identified?

q.en:
You are leading a software development project. A senior stakeholder requests a major feature change near the end of the execution phase.

What should you do FIRST?

en: Implement the change if it adds value
C. Review the change request through the integrated change control process
Escalate the request to the sponsor.
Inform the team to stop working until a decision is made

x.en:
In project management, particularly during execution, changes often arise. However, PMI emphasizes that any change—especially significant ones—must first go through the Perform Integrated Change Control (PICC) process. This process involves documenting the request, analyzing its impact on scope, time, cost, quality, and resources, and getting formal approval before implementation. This protects the project from uncontrolled scope changes, ensures alignment with the baseline, and maintains governance.

The PICC process includes tools like the change control board (CCB), expert judgment, and impact analysis. Skipping this process can cause budget overruns, missed deadlines, or dissatisfaction among stakeholders due to undocumented scope additions.

q.en: What is the main outcome of a Sprint Review?

en: An increment of the product
A sprint goal as agreed upon by the product owner and team
A prioritized list of backlog items
The team finalizes the Sprint Backlog for the next Sprint.

x.en:
🔹 Domain: Process

🔹 Approach: Agile

🔹 Importance:
Important, because it tests your understanding of Scrum events and the distinction between Sprint Review, Sprint Planning, Increment, and Product Backlog updates.

🔹 Keywords:
Sprint Review – sprint goal – product owner – team

The Sprint Review is held to inspect what was completed during the Sprint and determine whether the Sprint Goal was achieved, while gathering stakeholder feedback and discussing what to do next.
In this question, the best answer is the sprint goal as agreed upon by the product owner and team, because the essence of the Sprint Review is checking completed work against the agreed goal.

It is important to distinguish among these ideas:

 The increment is produced during the Sprint
 Product Backlog reprioritization may be influenced by the review
 The next Sprint Backlog is finalized during Sprint Planning
 The Sprint Review focuses on completed work and goal achievement

🔹 Example:
A team is building a banking app, and the Sprint Goal is enabling fingerprint login. During the Sprint Review, the team demonstrates the feature to the product owner and stakeholders to confirm the goal was actually achieved. The main outcome here is validation of the Sprint Goal, not finalizing the next Sprint Backlog.

🔹 Exam Tips:
If you see Sprint Review, think of demonstrating completed work, inspecting the goal, and collecting stakeholder feedback.
If the option mentions Increment only, be careful because the increment is a Sprint deliverable, not the meeting outcome itself.
If the option mentions finalizing the next Sprint Backlog, that points to Sprint Planning.
If the exam rephrases the question as What does the team inspect with stakeholders at the end of the Sprint? the answer will likely relate to completed work or Sprint Goal achievement.
If it asks What is updated after the Sprint Review? the answer may be the Product Backlog, not the Sprint Goal.

q.en:
A customer wants the development of a core component to be based on agile practices, as the final scope of the requirement has not yet been fully developed. The project manager is participating in contract development with the sales team and wants to ensure that development costs do not impact the profitability of the project.

Which two controls should the project manager incorporate in the contract for the development of the core component? (Choose 2)

en: Establish a governance committee to review the contract delivery
Identify or separate fixed and agile components
Provide alternatives to scope change at specific project phases within the contract
Require only internal resources be utilized for this project
Specify the number of iterations for development in the contract

x.en:
Domain:
Process 

🔹 Approach:
Hybrid

🔹 Importance:
Very important, because it tests how contracts are structured in agile or hybrid environments and how the project manager protects profitability when final scope is not fully defined.

🔹 Keywords:
core component – agile practices – final scope – contract development – profitability

This question is about selecting appropriate contractual controls when the customer wants a core component developed using agile practices because the final scope is not yet fully defined.
The challenge is not just delivering the work, but doing so in a way that preserves flexibility without losing control over cost and profitability.

That is why the best two controls are:

First: specify the number of iterations in the contract
This prevents development from continuing in an uncontrolled manner. In agile work, the customer may keep requesting refinements or changes, so defining a limited number of iterations creates a clear financial and time boundary.

Second: identify or separate fixed and agile components
Some parts of the project may already be well defined and can be treated as fixed components, while other parts are still evolving and can be managed using agile methods. This distinction reduces ambiguity and makes the contract more balanced between flexibility and control.

This reflects adaptive contracting logic in agile, where not everything is fixed upfront, but clear boundaries and controls are still needed to prevent profitability erosion.

🔹 Example:
A software company signs a contract to build a digital platform. One core area, such as authentication integration and security rules, is already well defined and can be treated as fixed. But user interface refinements and optimization features are still evolving, so they are handled in an agile way.
The contract states that only 6 iterations are included for the evolving work and clearly separates the fixed elements. This allows flexibility without leaving cost unlimited.

🔹 Exam Tips:
If the question mentions agile contracting, incomplete scope, and profitability or cost, think about controls that prevent unlimited openness.
If an option sets boundaries on iterations, time, or cost, it is often closer to the correct answer.
If an option separates fixed and variable parts, it usually reflects strong hybrid contracting logic.
If an option focuses only on internal resources or only on governance committees, it is usually less direct than actual contractual controls.
If the wording changed to a fully predictive environment with clearly defined scope, the answer might shift more toward a fixed-price contract rather than iteration control.

 PMBOK 7th Edition: Pages 129–136
 PMBOK 6th Edition: Pages 471–489
 Agile Practice Guide: Pages 77–81, 131–134
 ECO 2026: Pages 14–18

q.en: Scrum users must frequently review Scrum artifacts and progress toward a Sprint Goal to detect undesirable variances. Which pillar of Scrum does this represent

en: Inspection
Transparency
Adaptation
Sprint

x.en:
Scrum has 3 Pillars.

1- Transparency Significant aspects of the process must be visible to those responsible for the outcome. Transparency requires those aspects be defined by a common standard so observers share a common understanding of what is being seen. For example: A common language referring to the process must be shared by all participants; and, Those performing the work and those inspecting the resulting increment must share a common definition of "Done".

2- Inspection Scrum users must frequently inspect Scrum artifacts and progress toward a Sprint Goal to detect undesirable variances. Their inspection should not be so frequent that inspection gets in the way of the work. Inspections are most beneficial when diligently performed by skilled inspectors at the point of work. 

3- Adaptation If an inspector determines that one or more aspects of a process deviate outside acceptable limits and that the resulting product will be unacceptable, the process or the material being processed must be adjusted. An adjustment must be made as soon as possible to minimize further deviation.

q.en: Agile team members are estimating how long it would take to develop features for a new application without being overly concerned about accuracy. A new team member is concerned that a lack of planning now would cause scheduling problems later on. What is the best advice that the agile practitioner can give to this new team member on agile sizing and estimating the project duration

en: Once the velocity is established, the total amount of story points divided by velocity will determine the project duration
To determine the project duration , velocity should be calculated prior to the start of the first iteration.
Project duration is determined using bottom-up estimating by adding up the duration of the tasks comprising the user stories
The project duration can be determined by adding the number of story points completed by the team in each iteration.

x.en: Hint: In Agile, project duration cannot be accurately estimated up front. Rather, it can be derived from observing the team performance and knowing the total amount of story points. "The duration of a project is not estimated as much as it is derived by taking the total number of story points and dividing it by the velocity of the team." Velocity can be roughly estimated at the beginning of the project if the project uses the same team, same (or similar) technologies, and other team and project attributes that are same or similar to the previously completed projects. If the velocity cannot be estimated based on those factors, it should be observed during the first two to three iterations. Once the velocity is established and the total amount of the story points is known, this amount can be divided by the current team's velocity to arrive at how many iterations it will take for the team to complete the project work. Iterations are time-boxed intervals, for example, two weeks. Knowing the number of the iterations, the team will be able to tell how long the project will take. For example, with ten 2-week iterations, the project duration will be 20 weeks. . Velocity is usually known after the team has run a few iterations (typically two to three). Dividing the total amount of story points by velocity would result in the number of iterations required to complete the project. With a time-boxed iteration length (for example 2 weeks), an estimated project duration can then be calculated.
