Prioritization
Sizing the story

x.en: MoSCoW prioritization, also known as the MoSCoW method or MoSCoW analysis, is a popular prioritization technique for managing requirements. ... The acronym, MoSCoW, stands for 4 different categories of initiatives: must-haves, should-haves, could-haves, and will not have at this time.

q.en: Which three of the following are impediments the scrum master should pay attention to? Choose three

en: A team member talking about a user story that is not on the scrum board
A review of the backlog at daily standup meetings.
A technology that blocks agile capabilities
A lack of team empowerment and an inability to self-organize.
A team member is talking about a user story that is on the scrum board.

x.en:
The impediments are Actions that slow down or hinder progress. The Three impediments are: 

1- A lack of team empowerment and an inability to self-organize. 

2- A technology that blocks agile capabilities. 

3-A team member talking about a user story that is not on the scrum board.

q.en: Which of the following arrangements allows least flexibility to the buyer to alter the contracted scope of works?

en: Fixed-price arrangements.
Not-to-exceed time and materials arrangement.
Dynamic scope option.
Early cancellation option.

x.en: A not-to-exceed time and materials allows replacing original scope with new scope. The dynamic scope option allows scope adjustments at specified points in the project. The early cancellation option allows termination halfway through the project. The fixed-price arrangement is the least flexible option. [Agile Practice Guide, 1st edition, Page 78]

q.en: Which of the following terms refers to the deferred cost of work not done at an earlier point in the product life cycle?

en: Opportunity cost
Net present value
Technical debt
Sunk cost

x.en: Technical debt refers to the deferred cost of work not done at an earlier point in the product life cycle. [Agile Practice Guide, 1st edition, Page 154]

q.en: An Agile team is progressing a little slower than what was planned at the start of the iteration. Which of the following Agile metrics will this effect?

en: Story points
Ideal time
Velocity
Actual duration

x.en: Story points and ideal time are sizing/estimating metrics; these do not change with actual performance. Velocity, however, would get reduced if the team is delivering fewer story points than planned. Actual duration is an absolute number you get at the end of an activity, it can be different than the planned duration, but the final value doesn’t change. [Agile Practice Guide, 1st edition, Page 61]

q.en: A Project manager is in the middle of an agile project comprised of 100 user stories broken down into five iterations . Each user story is worth 50$ . The actual expenditure is 2,000$ and 50 user stories have been delivered. How is the project performing.

en: The project is under budget and on schedule
The project is over budget and behind schedule
The project is under budget and behind schedule
The project is on budget and on schedule

x.en:
EV = 50*50 = 2500 , AC = 2000 

CV =EV-AC= 2500-2000 = + 500 so The project is under budget 
 

 The Project is the middle = 1/2 *100 = 50 user stories 

PV = 50*50 = 2500
SV= EV-PV = 2500-2500 = 0 so The project is on the schedule .

q.en: A project manager is leading a technically complex project. The project is part of a strategic program of work and the first to use an agile approach. One of the board members is interested in attending a meeting to see how the delivery of the project scope is progressing. What should the project lead do ?

en: Invite the board member to the next sprint review
Invite the board member to the next daily standup
Invite the board member to the next sprint planning
Invite the board member to the next sprint retrospective

x.en: Keyword (how the delivery of the project scope is progressing) so the best option sprint review . Sprint review : is held at the end of a sprint , during which the team demonstrate what was accomplished and give feedback .

q.en: A scrum team is midway into a sprint when the project sponsor approaches the scrum master and requests that a new , urgent , and potentially complex mandatory compliance -related requirement should be developed immediately in the current sprint . The sponsor stresses that if the requirement is not implemented , the entire project may be canceled . What is the scrum master's best response?

en: Discuss the requirements with the product owner , and let them make a decision , including sprint cancellation
Add the requirement to the current sprint backlog and direct the team to start working on it immediately.
Add the requirement to the product backlog and request the product owner to review the requirement after the sprint is over.
Submit a change request to update the scope baseline and add the requirement to the requirement traceability matrix.

x.en: The product owner is the appropriate authority to review new requirements and decide, together with the team, whether the requirements should be included in the prodcut backlog and in what sprint. The product owner may decide to cnacel the current sprint and start a new sprint that includes this new high priority requirement. In this case the teaة likely needs time to asses the impact of the new mandatory compliance- related requirement. The scrum master should discuss the new requirement with the product owner who , together with the team , may decide to cancel the sprint.

q.en: A project team is currently building a warehouse management system . Due to the complexity of the project and ambiguous requirements, the team decided to adopt an Agile management approach. If a higher rate of management process improvement is required by the project team, which of the following can help achieve this objective?

en: Adopting XP for the development phase
Frequent retrospectives and selecting improvements
Deferring the development until all requirements have been collected
Using a Kanban board to enable visual management

x.en: Keyword (Agile - Improve ) . Retrospectives can really facilitate process improvement by allowing the team to brainstorm on what went well and what went wrong [Agile Practice Guide, 1st edition , Page 32].

q.en: You and your team are executing the first Agile project in the organization. This is a special project for the organization as Agile is being piloted for the first time . You are nearing the end of the first iteration on the project and not all of the assigned user stories are complete. Can the team extend the iteration duration by a couple of days in order to complete all assigned stories in the iteration plan?

en: Yes, but requires the approval of the product owner.
No, the iterations are time-boxed
Yes, but requires the approval of the scrum master
Yes, but the extension cannot be more than 2 days

x.en: Agile is time boxed so the iteration durations cannot be extended. All incomplete stories need to be returned to the product backlog where they will get re-prioritized along with the other stories in the backlog. [Agile Practice Guide, 1st edition, Page 25]

q.en: The product owner has requested some major changes that will have a significant impact on the project and require reprioritizing the remaining backlog items. What should you do?

en: Cancel the current sprint and immediately call a retrospective
Terminate the current sprint and re-prioritize the entire project.
Complete the started stories but do not bring any more "Ready" stories into "WIP"
Complete the current iteration, re-prioritize the backlog and adapt the new plan for the next iteration.

x.en: Agile teams typically don't adjust their long term plan during a sprint unless all of the items being. Developed are dropped from the backlog. It is recommended to complete the current sprint and then re-plan and adjust accordingly. [Agile Practice Guide , 1st edition, Page 25]

q.en: Project life cycles can be shown on a continuum ranging from predictive cycles on one end, to Agile cycles on the other end , with more iterative or incremental cycles in the middle. Another approach is to visualize the continuum with a two-dimensional chart with the frequency of delivery on the Y-axis and the degree of change on the X-axis . What project life cycle should be proposed for the quadrant with a high degree of change and high frequency of delivery

en: Iterative
Agile
Incremental
Predictive

x.en: The Agile approach is recommended for projects that require a high degree of change and high frequency of project deliveries [Agile Practice Guide, 1st edition, Page 19]

q.en: Agile teams use which of the following to collaboratively prioritize user stories based on their respective value to the project's customer

en: Retrospective
Rolling wave planning
Backlog refinement
Kanban Board

x.en: Refinement Backlog / Backlog grooming involves adding, removing and prioritizing stories in the product backlog. The purpose of refinement is to help the team understand whay the stories are and how large the stories are in relation to each other. [Agile Practice Guide, 1st edition , Page 52]

q.en: A project team is currently analyzing its current iteration progress and reviewing the following chart. What is this chart called?

en: Control Chart
Burnup Chart
Histogram
Burndown Chart

x.en:
A burndown chart is a graphical representation of work left to do versus time. The outstanding work is shown on the vertical axis and time along the horizontal. It is useful for predicting when all of the work will be completed.

[PMBOK Guide ,6th edition, Page 226 ]

q.en: If the deliverables will be produced using an agile framework . What strategies might be appropriate to gain formal acceptance of the product scope? (Choose two)

en: Have the team demonstrate the completed user stories to the product owner at the end of each iteration
Ask the product owner to attend each sprint retrospective to review and approve the completed product increment
Perform the validate scope process once the entire project scope is complete in accordance with the scope management plan
Conduct a demonstration whenever enough features have been developed to from a coherent set
Ensure that the product scope is fully decomposed down to the work package level during initial project planning

x.en: In flow-based agile , the development team will demonstrate the completed work once enough features have been developed to from a coherent set. Teams that use flow-based agile typically employ a kanban board to manage their workflow. In iteration -based agile , the project team should conduct an iteration review . During the iteration review , the project team demonstrates the completed work, and the product owner then accepts or declines the user stories.

q.en: A customer is concerned about the time required to complete a project is asking the project team to reduce the number of iterations required to complete the product. Which approach should the project manager take ?

en: Prioritize deliverables based on business value and define frequent releases
Ask the team to challenge the project estimations for faster delivery
Ask the team to raise blockers or impediments in daily meetings
Prioritize the tasks with high risks to reduce the number of iterations required

x.en: Prioritize deliverables based on business value and define frequent releases

q.en: In a fixed time and budget project the customer wants the development of a core component to be based on agile practices, as the final scope of the requirements has not yet been fully developed. The project manager is participating in contract development with the sales team and wants to ensure that development costs do not impact the profutability of the project. (Choose two)

en: Tier the contract or fixed and agile components
Establish a governance committee to review the contract delivery
Require that only internal resources be utilized for this project
Provide alternatives to scope change at specific project phases within the contract
Limit the number of iterations for development in the contract

x.en:
Keyword (a fixed time and budget project)

so the project manager should

 Require that only internal resources be utilized for this project
 
 Limit the number of iterations for development in the contract

q.en: Based on the management's expectations, they want to ensure that the deliverable of the first iteration helps the marketing team present the product prototype to potential customers. As a project manager, what should you do?

en: Ask the sponsor to prioritize some functionalities of the product
Identify the minimum functionality required for the product
Increase the details of the work breakdown structure (WBS) to minimize errors and delay.
Split the backlog into phases to ensure that the key features are delivered first.

x.en: The project manager should focus on delivering a minimum set of valuable features to satisfy early adopters

q.en: During the last sprint review , the main stakeholder complained that the product was missing many features they had been expecting. The project team argued that every incremental met the acceptance criteria and was approved by the main stakeholder. The cost perfromance index CPI of the project is 1.15 and the schedule performance index SPI is 1.43. What should project manager do ?

en: Analyze the reason for the gap in understanding with both sides with both sides and negotiate a solution
Ask the stakeholder to submit a change request to increase the budget and time for the modifications request
Ask the project team to perform the modifications since the project budget and schedule can support them
Explain to the stakeholder that since the acceptance criteria for every increment were met , the project can be closed

x.en: Without understanding the reason for the gap, the issue can occur again.

q.en: A team is holding the first demonstration of the software built to date on a medium -sized project the product owner has uncovered a number of issues they would like to be addressed before providing approval how should the project manager approach this problem ?

en: Refer the product owner to the signed business requirement document and explain that the current plan cannot facilitate these changes
Tell the product owner the issues will be addressed in the second version of the software
Refer the product owner to the change management plan , then escalate to the steering committee
Plan to address the issues through backlog grooming and incorporate them into the next sprint

x.en: Plan to address the issues through backlog grooming and incorporate them into the next sprint

q.en: During the third iteration , the team encounters a major delay that has not had significant improvements over the last few weeks . What should the project manager do ?

en: Request additional team members to help with improvements
Incorporate a predictive approach for this element
Retrospect frequently and suggest improvements
Implement mitigation strategies for this element

x.en:
Approach : Agile
Keyword: Improvements
The correct answer (Retrospective = Improvements)

q.en: The team has been working for two months and has consistently missed planned user stories . How should the project manager address this issue?

en: Engage in recruiting a highly skilled resource to reinforce the skills
Consider using a reward system to encourage timely delivery
Promote changing the iteration duration in order to commit as planned.
Ensure the sprint size is appropriate for the iteration duration

x.en: Project manager should Ensure the sprint size is appropriate for the iteration duration to avoid delay and delivery comply with consistent pace

q.en: After a couple of iterations , the project manager decides to present the product to a key stakeholder. The stakeholder's feedback is that the team missed the mark on many features. What should the project manager do to avoid this in the future ?

en: Incorporate design thinking practices into the project life cycle to better understand the product's personas and be more effective to match their needs
Schedule adequate sprint demos to gather early feedback from the stakeholders and adapt the plan accordingly
Evaluate the team's skills to look for someone with experience in product design and assign that person the task of rebuilding the product interface
Setup requirements gathering sessions with all key stakeholders to evaluate the scope once again and re prioritize the backlog based on the sessions

x.en: The sprint review meeting should be held after the end of each sprint and before next sprint planning meeting to gather early feedback from the stakeholders and adapt the plan accordingly.

q.en:
A company wants to increase the commercial value of one of its products in a highly competitive market. In order to do this, the company commissions a project to create a prototype. The team constructs the prototype incrementally.
Which action should the project manager take as a priority?

en: Implement a plan-do-check-act (PDCA) cycle
Emphasize the use of Kanban methodology.
Ensure the project sponsor is aware of the go-to market date
Deliver business value as soon as possible.

x.en: In order to increase opportunities and increase business value when building a prototype the focus must be on business value

q.en: A Scrum team is analyzing the burndown chart on day four of a 15-day sprint. The burndown chart is shown below. What should the team do next?

en: Continue with the sprint work as planned and keep monitoring
Continue with the sprint as the progress shows buffers for potential interruptions
Ask the product owner if some low-priority stories could be cut from the sprint
Ask the project team to select any additional stories as they have additional capacity than planned

x.en: It's just day 4 of 15 days sprint. it's too early to take any action. Monitoring will be appropriate

q.en: During the execution of a complex project , the project manager encounters numerous change requests from various teams. These changes may result in the project not meetig its objectives. How should the project manager ensure that these changes are managed effectively

en: Record the changes using the risk register and continue monitoring
Review priorities with the product owner to include the changes in the backlog
Deny the change requests and keep delivering the project as planned
Review the project and communications management plan with the main stakeholder

x.en: According to scenario, the changes did not achieve the project goals and it is required that he wants to ensure that the changes are managed effectively. Therefore, according to the agile approach, the project manager should review the priorities with the product owner to include the requirements in the product backlog.

q.en: A transportation company is transforming its operational processes and the main system this company uses to move freight. The scope statement is in place. An iterative delivery approach has been agreed by all stakeholders. What does the project manager need to do next to help the team understand the work that needs to be done?

en: Start working on the project management plan with work packages, a detailed schedule, and work assignments for team members.
Create the requirements management plan to outline how project requirements will be collected, analyzed, and documented, and then assign requirements to team members.
Work directly with stakeholders on the work breakdown structure (WBS) and assign tasks with a required timeline for each team member to start the work.
Work with the team to decompose the scope into a WBS and work packages in order to create required deliverables and timelines.

x.en: To help the team understand the work to be done, a plan is created to determine how requirements can be collected, analyzed, and documented

q.en: An agile approach is facing quality issues with every release, generating many production problems. What should the project manager do to fix the problem and improve the quality?

en: Create a reward system granting incentives to the team members who are able to catch more defects
Seek extra funding approval with the sponsor to replace junior team members for more experienced ones
Hire an external company to add an additional layer of testing , making sure that the final product is well inspected before releasing
Use the retrospective meeting to better understand the root cause of the quality problems and put together a plan with the team to address the problems

x.en: Quality issues with each release - improve quality so a retrospective meeting is best suited for this

q.en: Traditional project management approaches included multiple KPIs that predicted the success of a project. How do we demonstrate success of an Agile project?

en: By demonstrating that a working product has been delivered to the customer
By reusing the traditional KPIs and measures
By release on time
By maintain productive team velocity

x.en: Agile Principles (Working software is the primary measure of progress)

q.en: You are leading a project to design a new and innovative system based on newly developed technology. In past projects , using a traditional waterfall project management approach, you have encountered issues with scope creep. However , given the nature of the current project , you have decided to use an agile approach. As it telated to project scope, how will this project differ from your past projects?

en: The project scope will evolve during the project
During initial planning, more detailed work breakdown structure will be created
Scope creep will be avoided with a strict change management system
The project scope will be better understood at the beginning of the project

x.en:
In the scenario you have decided to use an agile approach which differ about Traditional approach
An agile approach is change drriven development approach
 the project scope isnot unclear in the beginning or not weel iunderstood upfront will evolve during the project
Traditional approach is plan driven development so detailed scope and clear in the planning phase

q.en: You are working on a project that consists of three releases , five iterations per release . The first release willprovide the must-have features required for a mininmum viable product with additional features added after each subsequent release. The customer wants to know which features will be available at the end of each iteration. What is the best tool or technique to use in this situation?

en: Activity list
Schedule Baseline
Critical path method
Agile release planning

x.en: Agile release planning is a project management approach where teams build and release products in iterations or incremental stages rather than all at once or grouped into distinct major releases

q.en: Which kanban key performance indicator allows teams to make reliable commitments about how long it takes them to deliver work?

en: Velocity
Cycle time
WIP
Defects

x.en: Cycle time refers to the time it takes for a work item to go through part of an overall process. Cycle time allows teams to make commitments how long it would take for the team to deliver work.

q.en: A product owner meets with the agile team and stakeholders to prioritize features in the product backlog. Each feature is categorized based on the risk associated with its development and the value the feature provides to the customer. Which features should the product owner prioritize to be developed first in order to maximize the probability of projct success?

en: Low risk /low value
High risk/High value
Low risk /High value
High risk/ Low value

x.en:
First High value , High risk
Second High value , low risk
Third low value /High risk
Fourth low value / low risk

q.en: To produce deliverables , your project has to contract with several vendors. The deliverables will be developed using an agile framework with constraint driven delivery , which will influence the contractual relationship with the vendors. Which of the following strategies would be the most appropriate for this project? (Choose three)

en: Pursue a shared - risk -reward relationship with the vendors
Utilize a standard firm-fixed price contract for each of the vendors
Adopt fixed-price increments when contracting with the vendors
Include an early cancellation option in the vendor contracts
Develop the procurement statement of work based on the detailed WBS

x.en: The question describes a project that will use agile methodologies, including constraint driven delivery . Constraint driven delivery is a common strategy for agile projects, where the cost and/or time are fixed, and the scope is allowed on vary. Such projects will require greater flexibility and a more collaborative relationship with vendors as compared to a traditional waterfall approach.

q.en: An agile project manager has contracted with a vendor some of the deliverables required for the project . The vendor is also using an agile project management approach to deliver their work. How should the progress of the vendor be assessed?

en: By attending the vendor team's daily stand up meetings
By reviewing the weekly progress report from the vendor
By conducting procurement audits of the vendor's processes
By reviewing the released versions of the vendor's work

x.en: In Agile project one of the 12 principles "Working software is the primary measure of progress."

q.en: Due to the lack of expertise , some agile project deliverables will need to be outsourced to external vendors. The performing organization wants to ensure that the selected vendor will use agile as their delivery method to produce the contracted deliverables . What is the best course of action for the project manager?

en: Colocate the agile project team of the performing organization with the project team of the be selected vendor
Develop the deliverables in house since this is always the best and cheapest approach to run agile projects
Select the vendor based on the best technical approach and lowest cost and set up agile training for the vendor
In the source selection criteria , specify that the vendor must use agile as their project management approach

x.en: it is a perfectly acceptable practice for the buyer to require that the seller's team members act much like an extended part of the buyer's agile team as part of the vendor selection criteria . Therefore , indicating in the source selection criteria that the vendor must use agile as their project management approach.

q.en: A company starts implementating Scrum . About halfway through the first sprint, communication issues develop. Some project team members are not in sync with other team members. What is the cause for this communication gap

en: Daily standup meetings were not held or enforced
The project sprint board has not been updated
The project status dashboard has not been updated
The communications management plan has not been developed

x.en: The cause for this communication gap is that the communiacations management plan has not been develope

q.en: As per the burndown graph shown below , the dotted burndown line is the plan. What should the team see at day 3

en: There is a cost overrun
They are at risk for that delivery
The iteration is ahead of schedule
The iteration on track

x.en: The graph shows an example of a burndown chart where the team planned to delivery 37 story points . Story points rate the relative work , risk and complexity of a requirements or story . Agile teams use story points to estimate effort . The dotted burndown line is the plan. The team can see by Day 3 that they are at risk for that delivery.

q.en: An agile team has been working overtime for the last few iterations . The project manager has decides that from now the team should maintain a 40-hour workweek. What is the most likely reason behind the project manager's decision?

en: To promote sustainable development
To minimize the amount of work in progress
To maximize the amount of work not done
To deliver working software frequently

x.en: Agile processes promote sustainable development . The sponsors , developers . The sponsors , developers , and users should be able to maintain a constant pace idndefinitely . " Constant pace would allow the team members to maintain their work-life balance, make fewer mistakes, sustain healthy productivity , collaborate better, and posiibly refrain from resigning.

q.en: You are a project manager for a construction project. During the project review meeting, the stakeholders decided to respond to known and new risks encountered during project execution. Which of the following artifacts should the stakeholders review?

en: Document management plan.
Risk-adjusted backlog
Assumption/constraints log
project log

x.en:
A risk-adjusted backlog is a backlog that includes work and actions to address threats and opportunities. Pmbok7 page#185.

The risk-adjusted backlog is a sprint or release backlog containing risk response tasks for actionable risks. For negative risks, these actions include avoiding, mitigating, and transferring. For positive risks, they include exploiting, enhancing, and sharing

q.en:
A company is changing their current business model. The change requires implementing a complex project using multiple agile teams.
What three options should the project manager have the testing team adopt as testing mechanisms? (Choose three.)

en: Security and performance testing
Tests based on behavior and test-driven development
Story testing
An experimental approach to cover all possible choices
Independent personal testing

x.en:
The three options should the project manager have the testing team adopt as testing mechanisms in agile teams.
A. Story testing
B. Tests based on behavior and test-driven development
C. Independent personal testing

q.en:
A customer's technical lead discussed a new feature with the project manager. The project manager believes the new feature will boost performance significantly and adds it as a high-priority item in the sprint backlog. At the end of the sprint, all of the planned stories were not completed because the new feature took more time.
What should the project manager do next?

en: Obtain approval from the project team and add the new story to the product backlog
Negotiate with the scrum master before adding the new story to the sprint backlog
Agree with the project team to modify and delete some of the stories in the current sprint backlog
Receive an agreement from the product owner and add the new story to the product backlog

x.en: The product owner is responsible for adding and prioritizing user stories in product backlog. Adding new features took a long time, which led to the incompleteness of all the planned user stories. Therefore, to get the team back on the right track, agree with the project team to modify and delete some stories in the sprint backlog.

q.en:
The project sponsor of a major initiative is consistently changing the prioritization of modular work packages. The team is used to three week sprints and is becoming increasingly frustrated with the daily changes in scope.
What should the project manager do?

en: Set up a meeting with the project team and ask for their opinion on what to do
Set up a meeting with the sponsor to explain the importance of keeping a strict sprint cycle
Decrease the sprint cycle to the average reprioritization request by calculating it in days.
Move to a Kanban strategy so that work can be reallocated more easily

x.en: The project manager should communicate with the sponsor and discuss the impact of the frequent changes in prioritization on the team's work and schedule. They should explain the importance of a strict sprint cycle for maintaining momentum, predictability, and accountability for the project, and find ways to align the sponsor's priorities with the team's work. This can help to mitigate the frustration of the team and ensure the project is on track.

q.en:
A team is finishing the third release to present to the stakeholder as part of a demonstration. The company that subcontracts the developers has communicated that there is a cash flow problem and the company will not be able to provide the same resources for the next iterations.
What should the project manager do next?

en: Analyze the impact against the release plan if the blocker is not addressed
Escalate the situation to the project sponsor for a possible resolution
Create a risk register to track the risks and request additional budget
Work with the project owner to prioritize the product backlog

x.en: Analyze the impact against the release plan if the blocker is not addressed

q.en:
A project manager has been assigned with initiating a large project to deliver complex equipment. Part of the project will be the result of a long research process, but once this is completed, the other part of the project must be incrementally delivered to the customer.
Which approach should the project manager choose for this project?

en: Adaptive
Predictive
Incremental
Hybrid

x.en: Adaptive is the correct answer. This is nowhere mentioned that the first part had a predefined scope. Since the first part was a long research, that has a high chance to be iterative and the 2nd part is evident enough to be increment. Both are the part of Adaptive but not Hybrid.

q.en:
A client wants to create an innovative software for the travel industry using an agile approach. A project manager from the company was assigned to work on the details and estimates as requested by the client.
What should the project manager do before sending the information to the client?

en: Put the tasks with estimates in the backlog and clarify that the project will not need any reserves
Work with the team to understand their views and add the appropriate dependencies and risks
Analyze the tasks, provide estimates, include a prototype demo, and send to the client directly.
Sequence the tasks with estimates and add standard risk reserves to use for software development

x.en: A client wants to create an innovative software for the travel industry using an agile approach so the project manager should Analyse the tasks, provide estimates, include a prototype demo, and send to the client directly

q.en: According to this burnup chart for the last 7-day sprint, what should the project lead address with the product owner and team?

en: The product owner should not ask the team to change their sprint commitments.
The team is accepting too much work in the sprint after it has started
The team is not meeting the expectations of the product owner
he team should have stopped on day 4 and started a new sprint

x.en: The burnup chart shows that the team is not on track to complete all the planned work by the end of the sprint. Therefore, the project lead should address this issue with the product owner and team and discuss the reasons behind the delay and the potential impact on the sprint goals. They should also consider adjusting the sprint backlog and priorities to ensure that the most critical items are completed.

q.en:
A project manager is working on an agile project in a changing business environment. The project sponsor is worried about benefits realization and asks the project manager to pay attention to changes that can affect the project.
Which action should the project manager take to identify changes that may affect the product?

en: Implement face-to-face communication between the team and product owner to change the iteration objectives as needed
Take action to re prioritize the backlog after every iteration to evaluate if user stories are still valuable to the business.
Apply a pair programming technique to react to changes immediately, even in the middle of the interaction
Stop the iteration as soon as possible in case an external change that makes the product invaluable is identified

x.en: To identify changes that may affect the product, the project manager should take action to reprioritize the backlog after every iteration. This will allow the project team to evaluate if the user stories are still valuable to the business and if they need to be adjusted or removed in light of any changes in the business environment. The project manager should also involve the product owner in this process, as they are the ones who are more familiar with the business requirements.

q.en:
A company has started developing a new product. During execution the project team notices that another competitor has launched a product with very similar functionalities and a cheaper market price.
What should have been done differently to avoid this scenario?

en: A minimum viable product (MVP) should have been released to get feedback from the market.
The Kanban method should have been utilized to optimize the work in progress (WIP).
An iterative life cycle approach should have been adopted
More backlog refinement meetings should have been scheduled

x.en: A minimum viable product (MVP) should have been released to get feedback from the market.

q.en: Which of the following techniques used in adaptive lifecycles helps in minizing scope creep?

en: User Stories
Product owner
Time boxing
Iterations

x.en: A timebox is a limited time period within which a well-defined deliverable must be produced with given resources. The deadline to produce the deliverable is set and must not be changed. The difference between a timebox and classical progress control is that when a timebox is used, the scope of the deliverable is one of the variables of project management. The quality, however, is never a variable. Time boxing helps to minimize scope creep as it forces the teams to process essential feature first , then other features when time permits

q.en: A project team has finished its first iteration out of six. The iteration's delivery performance (velocity) was 50% . During the iteration retrospective , the team realizes that the complexity of the work was underestimated . What should the project manager do?

en: Update the issue log and escalate it to the project sponsor
Ask to replace some team members with more experienced ones.
Ask the technical manager to help the team with the issue
Meet with the team to review internal actions to resolve the situation.

x.en: During the iteration retrospective , the team realizes that the complexity of the work was underestimated so the project manager should Meet with the team to review internal actions to resolve the situation .

q.en: A project team is conducting sprint planning. Based on the estimated effort,only 95% of the items included in the sprint may be delivered . The product owner asked the project manager for advice on how to prioritize the backlog items. What should be used to prioritize the backlog items.

en: Estimation accuracy
Risk to delivery
Business Value
Technical complexity

x.en:
🔹 Domain: Process

🔹 Approach: Agile

🔹 Importance:
Very important, because it tests how backlog items are prioritized in agile, especially when delivery capacity is limited during Sprint Planning.

🔹 Keywords:
Sprint planning – estimated effort – prioritize the backlog items

During Sprint Planning, if the team realizes that not all selected items may be delivered, the product owner should ensure that the most important items come first.
In agile, the primary basis for backlog prioritization is business value, meaning the benefit delivered to the customer or organization.

This does not mean risk, complexity, or estimates are irrelevant, but they are supporting factors rather than the primary prioritization driver.
The Product Backlog is generally ordered with highest-value items first, then effort, dependencies, risk, and feasibility are considered.

In other words:

 The product owner focuses on value
 The development team supports estimation and technical feasibility
 Prioritization should maximize delivered value

🔹 Example:
Suppose there are four features for an app, but the team can only finish three.
If online payment provides the highest direct benefit to customers and the business, while a color theme enhancement provides less value, the payment feature should be prioritized first even if some other items are easier or less risky.

🔹 Exam Tips:
If the exam asks how to order the Product Backlog, think first about business value or product value.
If the question is about what the product owner should prioritize when capacity is constrained, the answer is often value.
If the question focuses on what threatens Sprint completion, the answer may relate to risk, but this question is about prioritization, not threats.
If the question mentions effort or estimates, do not be misled; estimation is not the same as prioritization.
If the question is phrased as What should the product owner maximize? the answer is likely value.

🔹 References:

 Agile Practice Guide: Pages 18–19, 51–56
 PMBOK 7th Edition: Pages 9–14, 40–44
 PMBOK 6th Edition: Pages 138, 163, 167
 PMBOK 8th Edition: Pages 22–27, 64–69
 ECO 2026: Pages 10–16

q.en: An organization has historically executed most projects using a predictive approach. The organization now wants to change over to an agile approach . Due to this change , the project manager is worried about the scope definition process for upcoming projects. What should the project manager do to ensure the scope is completely defined?

en: Meet with the general manager and convince them to return to use the predictive approach to avoid any risk.
Help sponsors and stakeholders craft the product vision and bring the team and product owner together to clarify the expectations.
Ask the general manager to review every requirement to ensure that all projects will deliver the required products .
Ask the sponsor to increase a budget to check if every business needs are included in the requirements.

x.en: The project manager should help sponsors and stakeholders craft the product vision and bring the team and product owner together to clarify the expectations to ensure the scope is completely defined in agile approach.

q.en: A customer is concerned about the time required to complete a project and is asking the project team to reduce the number of iterations required to complete the product. Which approach should the project manager take?

en: Prioritize the tasks with high risks to reduce the number of iterations required.
Prioritize deliverables based on business value and define frequent releases.
Ask the team to challenge the project estimations for faster delivery.
Ask the team to raise blockers or impediments in daily meetings.

x.en: The project team want to reduce the number of iterations required to complete the product so the project manager should Prioritize deliverables based on business value and define frequent releases

q.en: An agile team is facing a challenge with the quality of its deliverables. Every time a feature is promoted to production, many defects arise, preventing the customers from properly using the solution. What should the project manager do to avoid this situation in the future?

en: Create a team incentive program with prizes, allowing the team members to work overtime to find defects
Reduce the release cycle and invest more time on the current features instead of releasing new ones
Hire a quality assurance specialist and integrate a second phase of testing into the current project life cycle
Use the next retrospective to understand the root cause of the quality issues and have the team come up with an action plan.

x.en: Many defects arise, preventing the customers from properly using the solution so the project manager should Use the next retrospective to understand the root cause of the quality issues and have the team come up with an action plan and to avoid this situation in the future.

q.en: A project team began working on a complex project that involves new technology as a product. The team is new to the technology and the proposed approach. Additionally, the customer is apprehensive about how the product will be received in the market. What should the project manager do to help the team and the customer?

en: Manage the risks associated with the proposed approach.
Assist the team with identifying the minimum viable product(MVP) to validate assumptions.
Work closely with the marketing team on market research and product segments.
Coordinate with the business unit to get detailed requirements.

q.en: A product owner presented the backlog to the team, and the team raised concerns over implementing some of the features due to various impediments. What should the project manager suggest that the product owner do next?

en: Ensure that the impediments are captured and prioritized based upon the highest valued features

Capture the impediments and inform management that their assistance is needed in resolving the impediments
Begin to remove the impediments, starting with the easiest ones first, to foster team accomplishment

q.en: A project manager wants to measure velocity as the indicator of the agile team's progress. Which of the following metrics is best for the project manager to use for this purpose?

en: The number of story points planned to be completed in the next iteration
The number of iterations completed by the team per release
The number of user story points completed by the team per day
The number of user story points completed by the team per iteration

q.en: A project manager has been assigned to a new digital product line, which the company hopes will boost their revenue. The product is complex and requires customer feedback to continually refine the product The project is being handled by across-functional agile team. What should the project manager do to ensure value is delivered quickly?

en: Identify tasks that can run in parallel to deliver the project faster
Plan the project to deliver value incrementally with regular releases
Ask the project sponsor to provide additional resources to fast-track the project.
Request a budget increase to pay the subject matter experts (SMEs) moreover time

x.en:
One means of delivering value sooner rather than later is via incremental delivery. Early and regular incremental releases lead to higher customer value and an increased market share.
Dividing the product into increments enables parts or elements of the product to be in the hands of customers prior to full delivery of the product.

q.en: A stakeholder requests John the Scrum Master, to show him the latest weekly status report to check the project's health and the remaining amount of work in the project. Instead, John takes the stakeholder to the team wall where a few pertinent updates are posted continuously. To address the stakeholder's query, John specifically points out to

en: Burndown chart
Sprint backlog
Kanban board
Velocity trend

q.en: A project manager working with the team to develop a software application. Due to failures in similar applications in the past, the rapid feedback from the customer on the suitability of the deliverables is very important. What is the best approach that should be selected?

en: Waterfall
Traditional
