ar: Scrum Master
مالك المنتج (Product Owner)
فريق التطوير
راعي المشروع
المدير الوظيفي

x.en: The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing value and ordering the product backlog. The Scrum Master facilitates and removes impediments; the Development Team delivers; the Sponsor funds and champions; the Functional Manager owns resources.
x.ar: مالك المنتج مسؤول عن تعظيم القيمة وترتيب قائمة أعمال المنتج. Scrum Master ييسّر ويزيل المعوقات؛ وفريق التطوير يسلّم؛ والراعي يموّل ويدعم؛ والمدير الوظيفي يملك الموارد.

q.en: Click in the correct spot: the region of the S-curve where the mitigation produced the LARGEST reduction in cumulative probability of cost overrun.
q.ar: اضغط في المكان الصحيح: منطقة المنحنى (S-curve) التي حقّق فيها التخفيف أكبر انخفاض في الاحتمال التراكمي لتجاوز التكلفة.

en: Region A — the steep mid-range around $7,000–$8,000 where the curves diverge most
Region B — the upper tail above $9,000 where both curves converge near 100%
Region C — the lower tail below $6,000 where both curves are near 0%
Region D — the extreme right where the curves meet
ar: المنطقة A — المنتصف الحاد حول 7,000–8,000 دولار حيث يتباعد المنحنيان أكثر ما يكون
المنطقة B — الذيل العلوي فوق 9,000 دولار حيث يتقارب المنحنيان قرب 100%
المنطقة C — الذيل السفلي تحت 6,000 دولار حيث المنحنيان قرب 0%
المنطقة D — أقصى اليمين حيث يلتقي المنحنيان

x.en: The mitigation's effect is greatest where the vertical gap between the 'before' and 'after' curves is widest — the steep middle of the S-curve. At both tails the curves converge (near 0% and near 100%), so the reduction there is minimal.
x.ar: أثر التخفيف يكون أكبر حيث تتّسع الفجوة الرأسية بين منحنى «قبل» ومنحنى «بعد» — أي منتصف المنحنى الحاد. وعند الطرفين يتقارب المنحنيان (قرب 0% وقرب 100%) فيكون الانخفاض ضئيلًا.

q.en: You are a project manager of XYZ project for organization. You and the Risk manager are establishing risk evaluation criteria for risk management process based on objectives and baselines to ----------

en: Measure the risk management performance.
measure the effectiveness of risk management process.
Enhance project success.
Evaluate the metrics

x.en: Establish evaluation criteria for risk management processes based on project baselines and objectives in order to measure effectiveness of the project risk process.

q.en:
AL-Habatrash is a huge Organization working in Construction by old style ,They got new project with Total Cost 18,821,540$  the customer requirements to work by the Up to date style and announced that the risk management very important for project success. Therefore the organization hired   a subject matter Expert to work as Risk manager during the project life cycle.

The Sponsor ,Project manager and the risk manager in the meeting ,then the Risk manager open the Lap top  to explain the benefits of risk management and how and when should be implemented, during the presentation the sponsor notice a complicated graphics ,he ask the Risk manager, what is this ,he told Mote Carlo Sampling technique as below.The risk manager explained the technique then the Sponsor asked him a questions, What is the probability to complete the project within budget?.

The values in the graph by thousands

x.en: The answer is 40% or P40 just from the graph you can see the percentage beside 18,821,540$.

q.en: In your organization you and your team studying the Critical Success Factor ( CSF.) of the  risk processes ,which of the following CSF of Plan risk management process.

en: Maintain risk awareness.
Iterative identification.
Use agreed upon approach
Project should be compatible with capabilities of people and facilities.

x.en: Critical success factors of plan risk management in the risk practice standard Chapter 4 page 22 . Comply with the Organization’s Objectives, Policies, and Practices. The rules and guidelines defined in the risk management plan should be compatible with the culture of the organization, its capabilities from the point of view of people and facilities, and its values, goals, and objectives.

q.en: You are a project manager of a new project. You are identifying risks on a project and decide to use a risk checklist to gather historical data from similar completed projects. which of the following should you include in the risk checklist? (Select two)

en: Previous project risks that may be relevant to this project.
The scope and cost management plans from past completed projects.
Quality analysis metrics from past similar projects.
Schedule variance from past completed projects.
Lessons learned from similar completed projects

x.en:
Previous project risks that may be relevant to this project and Lessons learned from similar completed projects.

Risk identification checklists can be developed based on historical information and knowledge that has been accumulated from previous, similar portfolios, programs, or projects and from other sources of information. The lowest level of a risk breakdown structure can also be used as a risk checklist. The reference is the standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs, and Projects, Page#131

q.en: You are a project manager of the NESs project in the organization FFA. You and the team members started risk identification using brainstorming with others. Who is the best to lead the brainstorming session?

en: Facilitator
Risk Manager
Project manager
Executive member

x.en: The goal of brainstorming is to obtain a comprehensive list of individual project risks and sources of overall project risk. The project team usually performs brainstorming, often with a multidisciplinary set of experts who are not part of the team. Ideas are generated under the guidance of a facilitator, either in a free-form brainstorming session or one that uses more structured techniques. PMBOK6 page #414

q.en: You are a project manager of a large project. You are evaluating some options to achieve the project schedule and budget. Each option's success is driven by multiple quantifiable factors. What should you do to evaluate and select the best option based on costs and probabilities?

en: Decision tree analysis.
AHP analytic hierarchy process
FMECA fault tree analysis
Sensitivity analysis

x.en:
The selection is based on the cost and probability. So, the decision tree analysis using the expected monetary value= P*I is the best to select the highest one.

Decision tree analysis: Causes the organization to structure the costs and benefits of decisions when the results are determined in part by uncertainty and risk • Solution of the decision tree helps select the decision that provides the highest expected monetary value or expected utility to the organization. The Standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs, and Projects, Page#152

q.en: You are a project manager of a new project for your organization JAL. You and your team identified all the risks that may impact the project if occur. You have called a meeting with a few experts with both software and hardware expertise to assess the impact of the technical risks reflected in the risk register. What risk management process are you most likely in?

en: Monitor and Control Risks
Perform Qualitative Risk Analysis
Perform Quantitative Risk Analysis
Plan Risk Response

x.en: You are conducting a risk probability and impact assessment which is a tool and technique of the Perform Qualitative Risk Analysis process

q.en: You are a project manager of a large project. During the planning meeting of the development of the risk management plan, the risk manager considers that risks may be identified that could also impact other projects in the organization. What should the risk manager do?

en: Discuss the matter with the risk managers of the other projects.
Address these risks on a partial basis
Document the impact of these risks in the risk register
Include an escalation process in the risk management plan

x.en: Escalation is appropriate when the project team or the project sponsor agrees that a threat is outside the scope of the project or that the proposed response would exceed the project manager’s authority. Escalated risks are managed at the program level, portfolio level, or other relevant parts of the organization, and not at the project level. The project manager determines who should be notified about the threat and communicates the details to that person or part of the organization. It is important that ownership of escalated threats is accepted by the relevant party in the organization. Threats are usually escalated to the level that matches the objectives that would be affected if the threat occurred. Escalated threats are not monitored further by the project team after escalation, although they may be recorded in the risk register for information. PMBOK6 Page# 442.

q.en: Eyad is a project manager working on a large project and finds several risks have a severity that is higher than the acceptable risk tolerance. They cannot be avoided or deflected. What response should he use?

en: Transfer the risk.
Mitigate the risk.
Change the risk tolerance of the client
Cancel the project

x.en: Eyad cannot Avoid or transfer(deflect) the risk, so he can only mitigate or accept, but in the options only mitigate available. So, he needs to mitigate to identify actions that will decrease the probability and/or the impact of a threat to be within acceptable threshold limits.

q.en: You are a risk manager who completed risk response planning for the project. The project is currently in the execution phase. During a periodic review of the risk register, the project manager recognizes that some key secondary risks have not been identified. Who is accountable for missing the risks?

en: The senior discipline engineers
The risk owners
The sponsor
The product manager

x.en: The risk owner monitors actions to determine their effectiveness and to identify any secondary risks that may arise because of the implementation of risk responses. The reference is the standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs, and Projects, Page# 38.

q.en: You are a risk manager of a large project. During a risk reassessment with the project team and external stakeholders, A key external stakeholder is overemphasizing the impact of some risks. This has led to a conflict. How should you avoid this type of conflict in the future?

en: Hire SME to facilitate the reassessment to avoid any conflict.
Perform assumptions/constraints analysis
Conduct sensitivity analysis to check which risks have the most impact on the project.
Review the project charter to resolve the conflicts.

x.en: Sensitivity analysis helps to determine which individual project risks or other sources of uncertainty have the most potential impact on project outcomes. Pmbok6 page#434.

q.en: You are a project manager of a new project. your project is in the initiation phase. You have invited the project stakeholders to a meeting to share their thoughts that may impact the project in a positive or negative way. What will be the main output of the above meeting?

en: Qualitative analysis
Assess the project's success
Identifying threats and opportunities.
Assess the project’s impact.

x.en: The risks are uncertain events or conditions that may be threats or opportunities. You meet stakeholders to share thoughts that may impact the project in a positive or negative way. Therefore, the stakeholders are invited to a risk identification meeting to identify threats and opportunities.

q.en: You are a risk manager of a new project. You are facing resistance as the team members try to implement the project's risk strategy. Some members of the project team believe it is a waste of time and money. What should you do to handle this situation?

en: Escalate the concerns to the project sponsor
Meet with team members to address their concerns.
Implement the risk strategies
Cancel the risk management activities

x.en:
Meet with team members to address their concerns and convenes them that risk management is essential and valuable to the project's success. You have to Focus stakeholders on creating a culture of risk awareness.

Train, coach, and educate stakeholders in risk principles and processes in order to create a shared understanding of principles and processes, and foster engagement in risk management.

Exam content outline/domain1/task2&6.

q.en: A project manager for the construction of a power plant project. The project manager is reviewing the lessons learned from a previous similar project. The previous project was delayed due to the delay in the delivery of a Water turbine generator (WTG). Construction of the previous project had to be shut down unexpectedly to wait for the late delivery of the WTG. What should the risk manager do first?

en: Record the risk in the register and communicate with the stakeholders
Meet with the previous project’s client.
Meet the other project manager to know the fact
Revise the project schedule

x.en: Record the risk in the register and communicating with the stakeholders is the first step then analyze the risk and assign appropriate responses to avoid or mitigate the risk.

q.en: You are a project manager for the construction of a new hospital. You request the risk manager to perform the initial risk assessment for the project that is about to kick off. Which of the following artifacts will help the risk manager to conduct the above analysis? (Select two)

en: Interviews and brainstorming
Sensitivity analysis
Configuration management plan
Work breakdown structure
Project organizational chart

x.en:
The Best Options
1-Work breakdown structure
2-Project organizational chart.

q.en: You are a risk manager for an infrastructure project. You are gathering and analyzing the performance data. You would like to identify which variables will impact the schedule and determine how these factors interact. Which data analysis tool should you use to forecast future performance?

en: Sensitivity analysis
Decision tree analysis.
What-if scenario analysis
Regression analysis

x.en:
Sensitivity analysis helps to determine which individual project risks or other sources of uncertainty have the most potential impact on project outcomes. It correlates variations in project outcomes with variations in elements of the quantitative risk analysis model.

Correlation in the sensitivity analysis is used in the model to indicate this relationship (how these factors interact).

In particular, given the uncertainty of forecasting, we need to “sensitize” the variables we use – to determine how far they impact the outputs we identify. To do this, we can run a sensitivity analysis.

q.en: A risk manager is working with the project team members on the plan risk responses process. Which risk response will likely cause a project to use the procurement processes?

en: Escalate.
Sharing
Acceptance
Engagement

x.en: Sharing involves transferring ownership of an opportunity to a third party so that the third-party shares some of the benefit if the opportunity occurs. It is important to carefully select the new owner of a shared opportunity to ensure capture of the opportunity for the benefit of the portfolio, program, or project. Risk sharing often involves payment of a risk premium to the party taking on the opportunity. The reference is the standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs, and Projects, Page#37.

q.en: Ibrahim is a project manager of the Cell phone project in the organization XUZ Inc. He came back from vacation; he wants to see the risk report. Which document he should see?

en: Risk register
Risk management plan
RBS
Communication management plan

x.en: The best document that has full information and update is the risk register, all changes during vacation are included in the register. If you check the contents of the communication management plan there are no reports available

q.en: You are a project manager for a project that has a significant impact on the organization. The organization’s risk appetite is low. Several stakeholders were concerned regarding the overall project risk during the development of the risk management plan. What should the risk manager monitor closely?

en: Risk response plans
Risk thresholds
RBS
Risk management log

x.en: The organization’s risk appetite is low which means the organization is risk-averse. The risk manager should monitor the Risk thresholds closely to keep the overall risk within the accepted level.

q.en: A risk manager of a new project is facilitating the risk planning process with the project team members. The risk manager wants to increase the breadth of considered risks, and include high-level and strategic project risks. What should the risk manager do next?

en: Use sensitivity analysis
Use work breakdown structure
Use Monte Carlo
Use a strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats (SWOT) analysis

x.en: SWOT (strength, weakness, opportunity, and threat) is a technique that examines the initiative from each of the SWOT perspectives to increase the breadth of considered risks. It ensures equal focus on both threats and opportunities. This technique focuses on internal (organizational strengths and weaknesses) and external (opportunities and threats) factors. The reference is the standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs, and Projects, page#135.

q.en: At the end of the design stage, the project cost has increased to the amount of a capital asset project. The customer wants one final total project completion date without any extensions. How should the risk manager proceed?

en: perform risk qualification and update the results.
revise the change /issue register.
Update the risk register and prepare for the Monte Carlo analysis.
Quantitative analysis to update the results with the new risks

x.en: Update the risk register and prepare for the Monte Carlo analysis to know the current completion date and the contingency reserve required to achieve the required date.

q.en: You are a project manager for the construction of a new airport. During the monthly review meeting, the project sponsor wants to understand how the project team has planned to manage risks that were identified in the last meeting. What should you do?

en: Report the secondary and residual risks only if they occur.
Assign the liability of secondary and residual risks to the sponsor.
Include secondary and residual risks as part of the response.
Use Monte Carlo assessment to assess risk impacts

x.en: The question is about “how the project team has planned to manage the identified risks.” So, including secondary and residual risks as part of the response will indicate how they plan risk responses.

q.en: You are a project manager of a new power station project. A subcontractor working on the project may cause delays in the schedule. You have added this risk to the risk register and issued a change request. The project sponsor rejects this change request. What should you have done differently?

en: Conduct an analysis to affirm the request is valid before submitting.
Inform all stakeholders that the request is in process
Executed the risk response strategy and document it in the risk register.
Advise the customer and the project sponsor that the request is being submitted

x.en: You should have conducted an analysis to know the probability and impact of the new risk on the project objective and assign an appropriate response then get approval from stakeholders on the strategy and the actions before the submit a change request to integrate these actions in the project management plan.

q.en: You are a project manager of a home solar panel project. The project has many internal and external stakeholders including shareholders, community groups, electricity companies, and investors. What should you do when engaging stakeholders?

en: No need to engage the stakeholders since the project is small.
Consider stakeholders’ positions and opinions regarding the project's output.
Include all stakeholders in the board of directors.
Get approval on response strategies from all stakeholders.

x.en:
Stakeholder analysis results in a list of stakeholders and relevant information such as their positions in the organization, roles on the project, “stakes,” expectations, attitudes (their levels of support for the project), and their interest in information about the project.

PMBOK6 page#512.

q.en: Which one of the following is the best description of the risk Tolerant stakeholder?

en: Tend to be adaptable and resourceful, enjoying life and not afraid to take action or even thrill seeking. This can lead to a somewhat casual approach towards threats, as welcomes the challenge of tackling the uncertainty head-on.

Sees present risk-taking as a price worth paying for future pay-offs, seeks strategies and tactics that have high future pay-offs. They think abstractly and creatively and envisage possibilities, enjoying ideas and not being afraid of change or the unknown. For both threats and opportunities. He is quite mature, focusing on the longer-term and only taking action when it is likely to lead to significant benefit.

Implies being reasonably comfortable with most uncertainty, accepting that it exists as a normal feature of everyday life, including projects and business. Trends to take uncertainty in their stride, with no apparent or significant influence on their behavior and may appear balanced.
Uncomfortable with uncertainty, has a low tolerance for ambiguity and seeks security and resolution in the face of risk.

x.en:
Risk averse or adverse is a person or group who feels uncomfortable with uncertainty, has a low tolerance for ambiguity, and seeks security and resolution in the face of risk.

Risk Tolerant implies being reasonably comfortable with most uncertainty, accepting that it exists as a normal feature of everyday life, including projects and business. The risk-tolerant person or group tends to take uncertainty in their stride, with no apparent or significant influence on their behavior. Risk-tolerance may appear balanced, but progress cannot be made while remaining perfectly balanced.

Risk Neutral sees present risk-taking as a price worth paying for future pay-offs. Risk-neutral individuals and groups are neither risk-averse nor risk-seeking, but rather seek strategies and tactics that have high future pay-offs. They think abstractly and creatively and envisage possibilities, enjoying ideas and not being afraid of change or the unknown. For both threats and opportunities, this risk-neutral approach is quite mature, focusing on the longer-term and only taking action when it is likely to lead to significant benefit.

Risk Seeker tends to be adaptable and resourceful, enjoying life and not afraid to take action or even thrill seeking. This can lead to a somewhat casual approach towards threats, as the risk-seeker welcomes the challenge of tackling the uncertainty head-on.

q.en: You are a project manager of a new construction project. The risk professional is working on the risk categorization when the subject matter expert suggests categorizing the risks by their impact on the project objectives. Why should the risk professional use this way?

en: To address risks effectively by business units.
Determine where more attentive project leadership and organizational involvement are needed
Ensure the team identifies the specific causes of risks associated with project objectives.
Ensure that project priorities are being appropriately factored into risk response plans.

x.en:
Categorizing risks by their impact on major project objectives can help ensure that project priorities are being appropriately factored into risk-response plans. An RBS can help the team identify specific causes of risks (e.g., scope omissions, resource shortages, estimating accuracy, etc.) that may necessitate additional management attention, while a WBS breakout can effectively segregate risks and risk severities by functional discipline (e.g., software engineering, quality assurance, procurement, etc.) and/or project work activity (e.g., design, manufacturing, test, etc.) to determine where more attentive project leadership and organizational involvement is needed.

The reference is the Project Risk Management_ A Practical Implementation Approach 2016, chapter#3

q.en: What are the key success factors for the plan risk responses process?

en: Early identification, address threats and opportunities, address the interaction of risks and responses, and specify the timing of responses.
Multiple perspectives identification, appropriate project model, addresses threats and opportunities and addresses the interaction of risks and responses.
Agreed-upon definitions, define roles and responsibilities, address threats and opportunities, and address the interaction of risks and responses.
Agreed-upon definitions, define roles and responsibilities, address threats and opportunities, and address the interaction of risks and responses.

q.en: A project manager is interviewing the team members to ensure their understanding of the assigned risk responses as risk owners. he and the risk manager are working together to evaluate the risk responses to determine their effectiveness in the project. Which of the following tools/technique will help them in this scenario?

en: Risk audits
Prompt list
Reserve analysis
Brainstorming

q.en: While a project manager is working on risk management, the project sponsor requests a rapid and cost-effective way of establishing priorities for the project risks. Which risk process can satisfy the sponsor's request?

en: Plan risk management process
Identify risk process
Quantitative analysis process
Qualitative risk analysis

x.en:
The qualitative Risk Analysis process is a rapid and cost-effective means of establishing priorities for project risks.

Perform Qualitative Risk Analysis assesses the priority of identified individual project risks using their probability of occurrence, the corresponding impact on project objectives if the risks occur, and other factors. Such assessments are subjective as they are based on perceptions of risk by the project team and other stakeholders.

PMBOK 6 Page# 420.

q.en: A risk manager is working with the team in the qualitative risk analysis process, they have identified several risks with a low probability and low impact as the project is currently planned. The customer concerns because the impact and probability of these risk events may change as conditions within the project may change. The customer would like to know where will these risks be documented and recorded for future reference. Within the above context, what should the risk manager tell the customer?

en: All risks should be recorded in the issues log for future review and update
Risks with low probability and low impact should be recorded in a watch list for future monitoring.
Risks with low probability and low impact should be recorded in the change log for approval.
All risks should be documented in the risk management plan.

x.en: Risk probabilities and impacts are assessed using the definitions given in the risk management plan. Risks with low probability and impact may be included within the risk register as part of a watch list for future monitoring. PMBOK6 Page# 423.

q.en: The risk manager for a new project trains the project team in risk management. The risk manager directs the team around the document that determines how to identify and qualify risks as well as how to identify contingency plans. What is the above plan?

en: Project procurement plan
Risk management plan
Risk response plan
Human Resources Management Plan

x.en:
The risk management plan is a component of the project management plan that describes how risk management activities will be structured and performed. The risk management plan may include some or all of the following elements:

Risk strategy. Describes the general approach to managing risk on this project.

Methodology. Defines the specific approaches, tools, and data sources that will be used to perform risk management on the project.

Roles and responsibilities. Defines the lead, support, and risk management team members for each type of activity described in the risk management plan, and clarifies their responsibilities.

Funding. Identifies the funds needed to perform activities related to Project Risk Management. Establishes protocols for the application of contingency and management reserves.

Timing. Defines when and how often the Project Risk Management processes will be performed throughout the project life cycle and establishes risk management activities for inclusion into the project
schedule.

PMBOK6 Page#405.

q.en: Which of the following is the appropriate description of the work of the risk owner?

en: Defining the stakeholder’s risk appetite
Identifying the new risks in the identify risk process.
Responsible/accountable for managing risks and selecting a suitable strategy for each individual risk
Developing the risk management plan and creating a detailed description of risks

x.en:
A single risk owner should be assigned to every identified risk. Manage the corresponding risk through all of the subsequent Project Risk Management processes. Select a suitable strategy for each individual risk based on its characteristics and assess priority, ensuring that the strategy is achievable, affordable, cost-effective, and appropriate. He defines actions to implement the chosen strategy. These actions may be delegated to action owners as appropriate. Monitor actions to determine their effectiveness, and also to identify any secondary risks which may arise because of the implementation of risk responses. Ensuring that the risk response is effective and for planning additional risk responses if required. Assess the effectiveness of any actions, that out decide whether additional actions are required, and keep the project manager informed of the situation. The risk owner may choose to assemble a team to develop a response.

All identified risks are recorded, and a risk owner may be identified at the same time. The risk owner is the individual responsible for monitoring the risk and for selecting and implementing an appropriate risk response strategy. It is the responsibility of the risk owner to manage the corresponding risk throughout the subsequent risk management processes.

The Standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs, and Projects, page# 32.

q.en: You are a risk manager, and you want to define the risk thresholds. Which of the following options will determine risk thresholds?

en: The Risk Manager
Risk appetite of the key stakeholders
The project Sponsorراعي المشروع.
The value of the consequence

x.en: The risk appetite and risk attitude are used to set appropriate risk thresholds in any given situation. Risk appetite is an internal tendency to take risks in a given situation, and it reflects organizational risk culture and the individual risk propensities of key stakeholders. The risk thresholds are external expressions of risk appetite.

q.en: The project manager of a new project for developing an application to support auto driving. The project manager and the risk manager are in the meeting with the project sponsor and key stakeholders to discuss the project overall. During the meeting, they are informed that the transport authority is discussing new traffic regulations for the industry that could be in place before the project completion. Within the above context, how should the risk manager and the project manager handle the above situation?

en: They should ensure that the project complies with the current traffic regulations and laws.
Send an email to the traffic authority with the general information about the project.
Meet with the traffic authority staff in charge of the new regulations.
Ask the traffic authority on the website weekly.

x.en: Meet with the traffic authority staff in charge of the new regulations to inform them about the project and ask if the new regulations may impact the project or not. Then identify the potential risks that may impact the project objectives.

q.en: A project manager wants to test a new product prototype before conducting full implementation on the overall project. What is the risk response strategy the project manager chooses?

en: Avoid
Transfer
Mitigate
Share

x.en: In risk mitigation, action is taken to reduce the probability of occurrence and/or impact of a threat. An early mitigation action is often more effective than trying to repair the damage after the threat has occurred. Adopting less complex processes, conducting more tests, or choosing a more stable seller are examples of mitigation actions. Mitigation may involve prototype development to reduce the risk of scaling up from a bench-scale model of a process or product. Where it is not possible to reduce the probability, a mitigation response might reduce the impact by targeting factors that drive the severity. For example, designing redundancy into a system may reduce the impact of a failure of the original component. PMBOK6 page#443.

q.en: You are the project manager of a large project and want to communicate the risk probability and impact to the stakeholders. Which of the following are good examples for that purpose?

en: Sensitivity analysis, Probability distributions, modeling and simulation, and probability and impact matrix.
Plan risk responses process, Monitor Risks process, risk checklist, control chart, and Monte Carlo simulation.
Fagan process, control chart, Monitor risk process, assumption and constraint analysis, modeling and simulation, risk management plan, and risk register.
Fault tree analysis, risk checklist, risk assessment, regression analysis, and assumption and constraint analysis.

x.en: Sensitivity analysis such as Tornado can provide the risks with the highest impacts. Probability distribution will represent the probability. Modeling and simulation provide the overall impact and the probabilities of achieving the objectives. The probability and impact matrix provides prioritization according to the probability and impact scales.

q.en: You are a risk manager for a new construction project. You and your team want one tool/technique that can be used in identify and analyze risks. What is this tool/technique?

en: Probability and impact matrix
Expert judgment
Monte Carlo
Trend analysis

x.en: Expert Judgment is a tool/technique in both processes identifying risk process and analyzing risk process.

q.en: You’re a project manager have completed three projects all with similar scope. You have recently been assigned to manage a new project and believe some risks may occur again on this project. What should you do?

en: Discuss and evaluate the identified risks with the project team members
Advise the project sponsor that these risks should be recorded as per the experience
Documents the risks in the risk register and calculates a contingency reserve
Implement the risk strategies into the risk plan

x.en: The new project may be different and you have to follow the risk management best practices. So, Discuss and evaluate the identified risks with the project team members first.

q.en: You are a project manager of a mega project. You have noticed that multiple new risks have come upon a project that was not included on the risk register. You discuss with the team to explain that risk management is essential for the project’s success, and risk identification is key. What should you do next?

en: Conduct the risk response plans
Perform an iterative approach to risk identification
Perform assumptions and constraints.
Assess the probability and impact of the project risks

x.en:
Identify Risks is an iterative process , a key success factor in the identify risk process.
since new individual project risks may emerge as the project progresses through its life cycle and the level of overall project risk will also change. The frequency of iteration and participation in each risk identification cycle will vary by situation, and this will be defined in the risk management plan. PMBOK6 #411.

q.en: Which of the following actions should the risk manager take when conducting a risk identification exercise? (Select two)

en: Ensure participants review relevant documents before attending the meeting
schedule a team meeting to discuss dependency mapping
Request additional contingency/management reserve from management
Ensure that all the relevant stakeholders participate
Update the risk register during the team meeting

x.en:
Ensure participants review relevant documents before attending the meeting.
	 
	 Ensure that all the relevant stakeholders participate.
	
	Exam content outline domain2/task1.

q.en: What is the total expected monetary value of the following?

A risk manager has identified a risk that will negatively affect the antivirus project. The risk manager and the project team have decided to use an older encryption technology because of the high risk associated with the new technology. Which type of risk strategies are they using?

en: Accept
Share
Avoid
Exploit

x.en: They canceled the new technology because of the high risk associated so, they avoid the risk.

q.en: The risk manager has identified, analyzed, and planned responses to a project's risks. The risk manager is required to create a monthly report on the performance of the risk management. What should the risk manager consult for this analysis? (Select two.)

en: Change orders Backlog
Proximity dates for open risks.
Risks due to many claims.
Risks that have materialized and the overall risk profile
Number of cost baseline.

x.en: Risks that have materialized and the overall risk profile and Proximity dates for open risks are the correct answer.

q.en: You are a project manager of a new project. You want to promote a common understanding of the value of risk management among key stakeholders to perform risk management effectively. Which of the following groups you should provide them training to create this understanding?

en: Project team members and internal stakeholders.
Management and stakeholders.
Project team members and management
Customers and Management.

x.en: Key stakeholders are usually easy to identify. They include anyone in a decision-making or management role who is impacted by the project outcome, such as the sponsor, the project manager, and the primary customer.

q.en: You are a project manager for the construction of a new Power station project. One of the team members identified a risk early in the project but he doesn’t document that risk in the risk register, because he considered that risk is trivial. During the execution stage, this risk occurs and impacts the project objectives negatively. What could you do to avoid this situation?

en: Give the team member Monte Carlo simulation and probability distribution to avoid this situation
Give the team members a risk management prompt list early in the project to ensure covering all types of risks.
Meet the project team members early in the project to ensure that team members are familiar with risk identification requirements
Cancel the risk management process

x.en: As a precondition for a successful Project Risk Management implementation, it is important to have a clear understanding of the risk thresholds that define the key stakeholders’ views on acceptable levels of risk, as well as a framework against which identified risks can be assessed.

q.en: How can the responses be carried out as a part of the project execution?

en: By continuous monitoring and controlling
By integrating the actions of the responses in the project management plan
By agreed upon approach and definitions
By effective communication.

x.en: Once risk response planning has been carried out, the project schedule should include all of the agreed-upon, response-related actions so that they can be carried out as a normal part of project execution and tracked accordingly.

q.en: A risk manager is working with the team in identifying the risk process. After identifying the risks, what should they do next?

en: Monte Carlo
Develop the response plans
Perform a probability and impact matrix
Perform quantitative risk analysis

x.en: The next step is the qualitative risk analysis process. The probability and impact matrix is a technique in the qualitative risk analysis process.

q.en: What is the overall goal, when selecting strategies during the Plan Risk Response process?

en: Strategies with the least schedule impact
Strategies with the least overall impact on the organization's appetite.
Strategies with the greatest benefit to stakeholders
Strategies with a significant overall positive influence.

x.en: In general, responses should be appropriate, timely, cost-effective, feasible, achievable, agreed-upon, assigned and accepted. Any proposed risk response plan needs to be assessed against the following criteria: • Consistency with organizational values, project objectives, and stakeholder expectations; • Technical feasibility; • Ability of the project team or risk action owners outside the project to carry out the corresponding actions; and • Balance between the overall impact of the response on the project objectives and the improvement in the risk profile of the project.

q.en: You are a risk manager for the construction of a new seaport project. You successfully developed the risk management plan and the risk register. Furthermore, the risk analysis and the risk response planning are finalized to deal with the high and medium priority risks. How will you deal with the remaining low priority risks?

en: Escalate them to a high level.
Add the risks to a watch list for periodic monitoring.
Keep the risks in the risk management plan.
Document them in the risk register at the end of the project for future use.

x.en: Risk probabilities and impacts are assessed using the definitions given in the risk management plan. Risks with low probability and impact may be included within the risk register as part of a watch list for future monitoring. PMBOK6 Page# 423.

q.en: The sponsor asks the risk manager about the risks that have the greatest impact on the project. Which of the following helps determine the request above?

en: Prompt list
RBS
Scenario analysis.
Sensitivity Analysis.

x.en: Sensitivity analysis helps to determine which individual project risks or other sources of uncertainty have the most potential impact on project outcomes. Pmbok6 page#434.

q.en: You are a project manager for an infrastructure project. The project has assumptions about the site conditions and has economic, technical, and environmental constraints. What should you do next to determine the risk impact of assumptions/constraints?

en: Document the assumptions and constraints in the assumption log.
Document all assumptions and constraints in the risk register.
Document the risk impact of the assumptions in the risk register.
Document the assumptions and constraints in the project charter.

x.en:
The first step in the assumption and constraint analysis is “List the assumption or constraint”.

Another way of approaching assumption and constraint analysis is to use the following logic sequence:

1. List the assumption or constraint.

2. Test the assumptions or constraints by asking two questions:

i. Could the assumption/constraint be false?

ii. If it were false, would one or more objectives be affected (positively or negatively)?

3. Where both questions are answered “Yes,” generate a risk, for example, in the form: may prove false, leading to “effect on objectives”

The reference is the standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs, and Projects, page#130.

q.en: You are a risk manager for a new fire system project. You decide to mitigate risk on the risk register. From which of the following sources should the funds be drawn to cover this response?

en: Contingency reserve.
Alternative contingency reserve.
The sponsor fund.
Management reserve.

x.en:
The risk is already identified in the risk register, so it will be funded from the contingency reserve.

The strategies developed to deal with risks at the project level consist of activities guided by the risk management plan, budgeted accordingly, and funded by the project’s contingency reserve.


The reference is the standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs, and Projects, page#59

q.en: Fahad is a project manager for a big project. He is now in the control risk process, which of the following can help to evaluate his compliance in risk management?

en: Risk Audit.
Risk Identification.
Reserve analysis
Risk Analysis.

x.en:
A risk Audit provides a formal assessment of compliance with the approach specified in the risk management plan.

The reference is the standard for risk management in portfolios, programs, and projects page#154.

q.en: A functional manager in an organization has initiated a budget change request due to a shortage in his department budget. He asks the Executive manager to approve the utilization of a contingency reserve from one of the projects in its closing phase. What should the risk manager of the related project have done to prevent the above situation from happening?

en: Coach the project personnel on budget change requests.
Conduct the risk monitoring and closing process properly.
Develop an accurate project budget
Improve the Communications with the high management.

x.en: Performing the risk monitoring and closing process properly using risk reassessments and risk reserve and other tools will help to keep the budget adequate.

q.en: You are a project manager of a new hospital project. You are working on understanding the project risks. You work with the integrated project team to develop the risk response strategies for the Identified risks. How should you work with these risk handling strategies?

en: You should ensure the strategies are approved by the stakeholders.
You should review and revise the strategies periodically.
You should implement the strategies after completing the risk analysis.
You should implement the strategies immediately.

q.en: You are a project manager of a high-risk rating project. You were just informed that one of the key project resources has decided to leave the company. You have already identified this risk previously and had created a transition plan to enable another resource to do the same tasks. However, the transition of the responsibilities to the new resource will create new risks to the completion dates of other project related tasks. What should you do next regarding the new risks?

en: Escalate the new risks
Address these secondary risks according to the risk management plan.
Review and revise the risk management plan.
Accept the new risks as there is no risk response plan

x.en:
You have to address the secondary risk as a new risk (identify, analyze, and assign appropriate responses).

Risk responses, when implemented, can have potential effects on the objectives and as such, can generate additional risks. These are known as secondary risks and are analyzed and planned for in the same way as those risks that were initially identified. There may be residual risks that remain after the responses are implemented. These residual risks are clearly identified, analyzed, documented, and communicated to all relevant stakeholders until they are satisfied.

The reference is the standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs, and Projects, Page#37

q.en: You are a project manager of a new project in your organization Mega-Q. You identified the risks that may impact your project, now you want to assign a risk owner for each risk, who are the best to be Risk Owners?

Risk manager
Management
Project manager.

Team Project is the best for Risk Owners

q.en: A project manager of a new pipeline project. He has requested the risk manager to schedule an initial meeting with the project sponsor. The project sponsor requests a presentation of the risks that have the most positive/negative influence on the project objectives. What should the risk manager complete before the meeting?

Qualitative risk analysis.
variance analysis

q.en: You are a project manager in a multinational organization that spans different countries. Your project is the digital transformation of the organization. you have assigned a risk management team leader who is risk management certified. What should the risk management team leader do in the early stages of the project?

en: Implement risk responses as per the risk management plan.
Perform quantitative risk analysis.
Benchmark to an organization that has executed a similar project
Coach stakeholders on best practices to perform risk management.

The risk management team leader should start with the Risk Strategy and Planning. The first task is Performing a preliminary document analysis:
