Give examples of preliminary documents to review prior risk identification including industry benchmarks (if available), previous lessons learned, historical data, and the sources of the above information.

• Determine and assign who is responsible for the preliminary document analysis (e.g., project manager, risk manager, financial controller)

• Establish documents relevant to the risk process

Exam content outline/domain1/task1.

q.en: The project manager of a call center project is performing the risk audit. Which of the following describes the goals and objectives of the risk audit?

en: Examine the performance of the project team and implement the important changes to improve their performance.
Identify new risks and close the retired risks.
Examine and Document what went well and not so well with the risk management process, and risk responses and recommend improvement actions.
Reassessment the probabilities and impacts of the identified risks and update the risk register according to the policy of the organization.

x.en:
Risk audits examine and document the effectiveness of risk responses in dealing with identified risks and their root causes, as well as the effectiveness of the risk management process. PMBOK6.

periodic risk audits are performed to determine strengths and weaknesses in handling risks within the portfolio, program, or project. This entails identifying any barriers to effectiveness or keys to success in risk management, the recognition of which could help to improve risk management of the current or future portfolios, programs, or projects.

The reference is the standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs, and Projects, page#39.

q.en: You are a project manager of a construction project. During the project review meeting, you and the stakeholders are making decisions on how to respond to known and new risks that emerged during project execution. Which of the following artifacts should the stakeholders review? (Select three)

en: Change of estimates principles.
Risk-adjusted backlog.
Assumption log
Project change log.
Risk register

x.en:
Assumption log. An assumption is a factor that is considered to be true, real, or certain, without proof or demonstration. A constraint is a factor that limits the options for managing a project, program, portfolio, or process. An assumption log records all assumptions and constraints throughout the project.

Risk-adjusted backlog. A risk-adjusted backlog is a backlog that includes work and actions to address threats and opportunities.

Risk register. A risk register is a repository in which outputs of risk management processes are recorded. Information in a risk register can include the person responsible for managing the risk, probability, impact, risk score, planned risk responses, and other information used to get a high-level understanding of individual risks. 

PMBOK7 Page#185.

q.en: An organization has two projects X and Y. The project manager for project X was expecting the mobilization of scarce equipment from project Y. But a day before the mobilization was scheduled, the project Y project manager notifies project X's project manager that the equipment would not be available for two months. This has delayed critical milestones for project X. How should project X's project manager avoid this situation in the future?

en: Inform all organization project managers about the delay.
Develop a contingency response plan to implement when delays occur.
Request the other project manager to officially confirm the new date in writing.
Add the other project manager to the monthly reports.

x.en:
Develop a contingency response plan to implement when delays occur.

Some responses are designed for use only if certain events occur. For some risks, it is appropriate for the project team to make a response plan that will only be executed under certain predefined conditions if it is believed that there will be sufficient warning to implement the plan.

q.en: A project manager for the construction of a new hospital. A project team member wants to know how often your risk identification process will occur during the project. Within the above context, how often should risk identification take place?

en: Daily
Vary depending on the situations within the project.
Monthly
At the end of the project.

x.en:
Identify Risks is an iterative process, since new individual project risks may emerge as the project progresses through its life cycle and the level of overall project risk will also change. The frequency of iteration and participation in each risk identification cycle will vary by situation, and this will be defined in the risk management plan. 

PMBOK6 page# 411.

q.en: You are a risk manager managing risks in a construction project. During the initial stage of project execution, a new risk is identified, the chance of occurrence of this risk is very small and the impact would be low if occurs. What should you do with this risk?

en: Ignore this risk.
Request stakeholders’ approval about this risk.
Ask subject matter experts to add a response.
Add the risk on the watch list

x.en: Since the risk with low priority, you should add it to the watch list. Risks with low probability and impact may be included within the risk register as part of a watch list for future monitoring. PMBOK6 page# 423.

q.en: You are a risk owner of an identified cyber security threat on an organization with a large computer network. Although certain measures were implemented to avoid the risk, the cyber security threat occurs. The measures were partially successful and a new unknown risk emerges. What should you do?

en: Implement workarounds to eliminate or mitigate the impact of the threat.
Create an efficient cyber security solution quickly to mitigate the risk.
Escalate to the risk manager and wait for his instructions.
Perform an analysis to determine the root cause of the failed response.

x.en:
The risk owner is responsible for managing the identified risks that have been assigned to him only.

The cyber security risk was identified and has a response but the response was not effective or failed. He has to implement the fallback plan or contingency plan, not a workaround. So before escalating the case, the risk owner has to perform an analysis to determine the root cause of the failed response to create an effective one.

q.en: You are a manager of Company A. You sell equipment to Company B, the stakeholders in your company do not want the risk of transporting the equipment from Your company. Instead of that, they want company B to take responsibility and liability once the equipment leaves company A.

en: Enhance
Mitigation
Transfer
Exploit

x.en:
Risk transference is a risk response strategy whereby the project team shifts the impact of a threat to a third party, together with ownership of the response. Transferring the risk simply gives another party responsible for its management. The transfer involves shifting the responsibility of a threat to a third party to manage the risk and bear the impact of the threat occurs. Risk transfer often involves payment of a risk premium to the party taking on the threat. 

The reference is the standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs, and Projects, Page#36.

q.en: You are a risk manager working with the project team, senior management team, subject matter experts, customers, and other stakeholders in the identify risk process to identify the project risks. Which of the following tools can help you to identify the risks by project objectives category?

en: Risk breakdown structure (RBS).
Influence diagram.
Work breakdown structure (WBS).
Affinity diagram.

x.en: The risk breakdown structure (RBS) is a hierarchical framework of potential sources of risk. An organization may develop a generic or specific RBS. The RBS helps to identify specific risks in relation to its category and offers a framework for other risk identification techniques such as brainstorming. An RBS helps to ensure coverage of all types of risk and tests for blind spots or omissions. The Reference is the standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs, and Projects, Page#148.

q.en: You are a risk manager of a new university project for your organization. Now you are in the meeting with the stakeholders to get an agreement on the risk strategies. At the end of the meeting, which of the following will be an appropriate description of the risk responses?

en: Scheduled, budgeted, and easy to understand.
Appropriate, timely, effective, and agreed responses.
Scaled according to the project, addressing threats and opportunities, iteration.
Cost-effective, validated by sensitivity analysis and assigned to action owner.

q.en: You are a risk manager of a new project. You notice that most of the identified risks are threats. What should you do to increase the number of identified opportunities?

en: Perform the Delphi technique with experts who have identified opportunities in the past.
Conduct prompt analysis.
Use a strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats (SWOT) analysis.
Meet stakeholders who have a positive idea.

q.en:
A risk manager of a new project is asking the stakeholders about the acceptable levels of cost increases and schedule delays

What is the risk manager trying to know?

en: Risk threshold
Risk attitude
Risk Impacts.
Risk Factors.

x.en:
The risk manager is trying to determine the threshold. The risk threshold is the measure of acceptable variation around an objective that reflects the risk appetite of the organization and its stakeholders.

A key element of risk strategy is the establishment and monitoring of enterprise, portfolio, program, and project risk thresholds. Examples of risk thresholds include:

· Minimum level of risk exposure for a risk to be included in the risk register,

· Qualitative or quantitative definitions of risk rating,

· Maximum level of risk exposure that can be managed before an escalation is triggered.

The reference is the standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs, and Projects, Page#10.

q.en: Which of the following is developed along with all risk management processes and contains the results of qualitative risk analysis, quantitative risk analysis, and risk response planning?

en: Risk register.
Project charter.
Change log.
Monte Carlo

x.en:
The risk register captures details of identified individual project risks. The results of Perform Qualitative Risk Analysis, Plan Risk Responses, Implement Risk Responses, and Monitor Risks are recorded in the risk register as those processes are conducted throughout the project. The risk register may contain limited or extensive risk information depending on project variables such as size and complexity.

PMBOK6 Page# 417.

q.en:
Sara is a project manager of a new hospital project. The risk register is developed by the team members during the initial phases of the project. The register is reviewed by the team members. Responses are planned, reviewed again, and risks are prioritized. The project is completed then the risk register is reviewed during the lessons learned session. During the review, Sara noticed that the risk register was not updated, and 20 responses were not implemented during the execution.

Which of the following should have been performed during the execution of the project?

en: Qualitative risk analysis.
Plan risk responses process.
Identify risk process.
Control risk process.

x.en:
During the Risk monitoring and control process, periodic risk audits are performed to determine strengths and weaknesses in handling risks within the portfolio, program, or project. This entails identifying any barriers to effectiveness or keys to success in risk management, the recognition of which could help to improve risk management of the current or future portfolios, programs, or projects.

Risk audits are carried out in order to evaluate the following: Risk management rules are being carried out as specified, and  Risk management rules are adequate for controlling the work. 

The reference is the standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs, and Projects, Page#39,147.

q.en: During the execution stage of the project, you find a risk was identified early in the project, but now the risk is no longer applicable to the project. What should you do next?

en: Escalate to the sponsor to terminate the person who identified this risk.
Close the risk during the next risk meeting and keep it in the risk register.
Ignore the risk since it’s not applicable to the project.
Remove the risk from the risk register and inform the sponsor that it is no longer valid.

x.en:
If the risk becomes no longer applicable to the project, you have to close it and release the associated reserve.

Outcomes can also include closing risks that are no longer applicable and releasing their associated reserves.

q.en: You are a risk manager of a new project. You and your team are working on the qualitative risk analysis process. What is the advantage of grouping risks by common causes during this process?

en: It helps the team to create risk categories unique to each project.
It can lead to developing effective risk responses.
It helps the project team to identify all risks.
It helps to analyze the risk events effectively with low cost and efforts.

x.en: Risks can also be categorized by common root causes. Risk categories that may be used for the project are defined in the risk management plan. Grouping risks into categories can lead to the development of more effective risk responses by focusing attention and effort on the areas of highest risk exposure, or by developing generic risk responses to address groups of related risks. PMBOK6 page# 425.

q.en: A risk manager starts risk the identification process. When does the Identify Risks process take place in a project?

en: Throughout the life-cycle of the project.
At the Executing stage.
At the closing stage.
At the Initiating stage.

x.en: Identify Risks is an iterative process, since new individual project risks may emerge as the project progresses through its life cycle and the level of overall project risk will also change. The frequency of iteration and participation in each risk identification cycle will vary by situation, and this will be defined in the risk management plan. PMBOK6 #411.

q.en: You are a risk manager for an important project. You are reviewing the Monte Carlo schedule risk analysis model before sharing the results with the project manager. You notice that activity correlations were not included in the model. What is the effect of adding the correlation to the model?

en: Change the standard deviation of the model.
Decrease the project completion duration.
Includes more risks to the model.
Increases the probability of correlated activities finishing on time.

x.en: Two activities might be influenced by the same risk, or one element might directly influence others. This needs to be reflected in the risk model using correlation groups. Failure to include correlation in a risk model allows elements to vary independently when in reality this would not be the case. For example, if the risk “contractor productivity may be less than planned” was mapped to several activities in the risk model, then we should expect productivity for all activities on which the contractor was working to be similar. The absence of correlation reduces the spread of results calculated during the analysis, with random uncertainty in uncorrelated elements canceling out. In reality, risks are interdependent, and planned activities are also related. These relationships must be included in the risk model, creating correlation groups to link activities and risks that can affect each other. Such links might be driven by the existence of common causes or external dependencies, or where a single risk affects several elements of the model. In these cases, the Monte Carlo tool’s ability to sample randomly must be constrained.

q.en: You are a project manager for the construction of an infrastructure project. During the meeting with the project director and the board, you determined that the project has depleted the entire contingency reserve and has started eroding the profit margin. You request the risk manager to take full advantage of opportunities. Which of the following responses should the risk manager take?

en: Exploit
Catch the risk.
Transfer
Share

q.en: Mike is a project manager of a car project in Organization DELA. During execution he discovered a risk by himself and asked the risk manager for information about this risk, the risk manager informed him that the risk was not identified, what should the Project Manager do?

en: Hold a meeting with the sponsor.
Ask the risk manager to identify and qualify the risk.
Ask the Risk manager to do a workaround.
Document the risk and take no action since it was not identified by the risk manager.

x.en: It is impossible to know in advance all the risks that may occur in a project, therefore the Identify Risks and Perform Qualitative Analysis processes should be repeated periodically for individual risks.

q.en: You are a project manager trying to achieve benefits from new materials in an adaptive project. This is the first time the project team has used this type of material, so the team has no information to identify and analyze risks. A team member informs you that a local institute has recently published a research journal on the same article. Where should you find this information?

en: Enterprise environmental factors.
Industrial studies.
Organizational process assets.
Commercial risk databases.

x.en:
The enterprise environmental factors that can influence the Identify Risks process include but are not limited to:

· Published material, including commercial risk databases or checklists,

· Academic studies,

· Benchmarking results, and

· Industry studies of similar projects.

PMBOK6 Page#413.

q.en: Susan is a new project manager who has been assigned to an existing project in the execution stage, during the first meeting one of the project team informed her that there is a risk that may impact the project after two months. What should the Project manager do?

en: Review the Risk register.
Review the risk management plan.
Submit a change request.
Update Stakeholder Register.

x.en: Risks are documented in the risk register. Other details we can find in the risk register include the risk probability and impact, the risk owner, the risk planned response strategy, and the risk time frame. The best action for the project manager is to review the risk register to understand the details of the risk and the proposed response. Only after this analysis and the Project Manager  feels the response is not adequate can other actions be put in place.

q.en: Tom work as the project manager for KFS Inc. He is monitoring the project performance. He wants to make a decision to change the project plan to eliminate risk in order to protect the project objectives from the impacts. Which of the following strategies will you use to address the risk?

en: Risk mitigation
Risk transference
Risk acceptance
Risk avoidance

x.en:
Risk avoidance is when the portfolio, program, or project team acts to eliminate a threat or protect activity from risk impact. It may be appropriate for a high-priority threat with a high probability of occurrence and a large negative impact. Avoidance may involve changing some aspect of the management plan or changing the objective that is in jeopardy in order to eliminate the threat impact entirely. Should the risk materialize, it would have no effect with respect to the objective. The risk owner may also take action to isolate the objective from the risk’s impact if it were to occur. 

The reference is the standard for risk management in portfolios, programs, and projects page#36

q.en: Eyad is a risk manager of the MNM project for his organization MEKA. Eyad was on vacation and came back to his project. He observes during the status meeting that many activities that had been accomplished were not in the original plan. What should he do first?

en: Review risk activities.
Send an email to the customer.
Review the change control log.
Meet the team.

x.en: Since the activities weren’t in the original plan, so these activities are added to the plan by change requests. The best choice is “review the change log” to know the detail of the changes.

q.en: You and your team have completed the project management plan, and the plan has been approved by the stakeholders. The customer asks you if the project can be delivered one month sooner. The customer offers sufficient monetary incentive for you. you decided to fast-track the project. This decision will:

en: Not affect risk.
Increase risk.
Decrease risk.
Risk change cannot be determined.

x.en: Fast-tracking is a schedule compression technique in which activities or phases are normally done in sequence and are performed in parallel for at least a portion of their duration. Fast-tracking may result in rework and increased risk.

q.en: You are a project manager of a new project for your organization. During project execution, a previously unidentified risk has just occurred. This risk will negatively affect the outcome of the project. What should you do next?

en: Develop the contingency plan.
Workaround
Risk audit.
Cancel the project.

x.en: The Unidentified risks are handled by workaround if occur. Workarounds are responses that were not initially planned but are required to deal with emerging risks that were previously unidentified or accepted passively.

q.en: Mega is a construction company, you are the project manager for the ASD project. You and the audit team in your company are preparing a risk audit report, the CEO invited you, your sponsor, and the audit team for a meeting to discuss the Risk audit report. Which of the following reports will be discussed with the CEO during the meeting?

en: A summary risk audit report will be presented during the meeting.
Since the meeting for the audit, all projects progress reports and audit reports will be presented at the meeting.
Reformat the detailed audit report by using highlights.
Detailed Risk audit report will be presented during the meeting.

x.en: Top management always prefers summary reports, so option A summary risk audit report will be presented during the meeting is more accurate.

q.en: A risk manager has been informed that they cannot outsource work or eliminate the scope. They also cannot mitigate the risk or buy insurance. What should the risk manager do next?

en: Transfer the risk.
Motivate the risk.
Exploit the risk.
Accept the risk.

x.en: Risk acceptance acknowledges the existence of a threat, but no proactive action is taken. This strategy may be appropriate for low-priority threats, and it may also be used where it is not possible or cost-effective to address a threat in any other way. Acceptance can be either active or passive. The most common active acceptance strategy is to establish a contingency reserve, including amounts of time, money, or other resources to handle the threat if it occurs. Passive acceptance involves no proactive action apart from a periodic review of the threat to ensure that it does not change significantly.

q.en: A project manager is building a prototype board for a critical project. Since the organization lacks the required level of fabrication expertise, the project manager outsources the fabrication process for board development to an approved external vendor. During the project execution, the vendor informs the project manager of a probable one-month delay in the final delivery. What is the above situation?

en: Residual risk.
Secondary Risk.
Risk Origin
Risk probability

x.en:
The main response is transfer, but due to the implementation of the transfer, a new risk has arisen. The new risk is the secondary risk.

Risk responses, when implemented, can have potential effects on the objectives and as such, can generate additional risks. These are known as secondary risks and are analyzed and planned for in the same way as those risks that were initially identified. There may be residual risks that remain after the responses are implemented. These residual risks are clearly identified, analyzed, documented, and communicated to all relevant stakeholders until they are satisfied. 

The reference is the standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs, and Projects, page#37

q.en: You are a project manager for your organization. You and your team identified the risks and performed the Qualitative Risk analysis. Now you are in Quantitative risk analysis. The Sponsor requested you to determine the Risks that have the greatest impact on your project. You started the Sensitivity analysis and now you have the following diagram, Which of the following risks has the greatest impact?

en: Total capacity cost.
No. forced, sustained outages.
Duration per outage and Avg.
New customer connects rate and Avg.

x.en: It's clear from the diagram that “No. forced, sustained outages” has the greatest impact.

q.en: You are a project manager for an IT project within a portfolio that contains several projects and programs. You have identified one risk that is more than your authority. What should you do to handle this risk?

en: Cancel the project.
Meet with the project managers to develop a risk response strategy.
Escalate the risk to the portfolio level.
Ask for additional reserve from the sponsor.

x.en: Escalation is appropriate when a threat is outside of the portfolio, program, or project scope or when the proposed response exceeds a given manager’s authority. Escalated risks are managed at the enterprise domain, portfolio domain, program domain, or other relevant parts of the organization. Ownership of escalated threats is accepted by the relevant party in the organization. A threat is usually escalated to the appropriate level that matches the objective that would be affected if the threat occurred. The reference is the standard for risk management in portfolios, programs, and projects page #36.

q.en: You are a risk manager for an infrastructure project. You are in the qualitative risk analysis process assessing and prioritizing the identified risks. Within the above context, what is the description of R1?

en: A risk with low probability and low impact
A risk with a 10% probability and high impact impact
A risk with a 70% probability and medium impact
A risk with low probability and medium impact

x.en:
From the matrix:
the probability of R1 is between 0.6 and 0.8 in the high probability area and almost 70% probability. the impact between 0.4 and 0.6 on the medium impact scale.

q.en: Which of the following is a key success factor in Identify risks process?

en: Alignment with the internal and external constraints and priorities.
Specify the timing of risk responses.
Iterative Identification.
Balance between cost or effort and benefit.

x.en:
KEY SUCCESS FACTORS FOR IDENTIFYING RISKS

Early identification, Iterative identification, Emergent identification, Comprehensive identification, Explicit identification of opportunities, Multiple perspectives, Risks linked to objectives, Complete risk statement, Ownership and level of detail, Frequent and effective communication, and Objectivity to minimize bias.

The reference is the standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs, and Projects, Page# 33.

q.en: One of the stakeholders in your project wants an additional fund for risk strategy, but he does not know the amount that can be approved without high management's approval. Within the above context, where can he find the amount that can be approved without escalation?

en: Cost management plan.
Risk Register.
Risk management plan.
Project Charter.

x.en: The cost of treating the risks themselves should be included appropriately in the project budget, while the risk management plan should describe how this part of the project budget is evaluated, allocated, and managed. The risk management plan will define the monitoring methods to ensure that the corresponding expenditures are tracked appropriately, as well as the conditions under which the approved budget for risk management can be modified.

q.en: You have observed an unusually high rate of risks but you have limited resources to address them. Which of the following should you use to determine risk priorities?

en: Risk management plan.
RBS
Prompt lists.
Risk probability and impact matrix.

x.en: A probability and impact matrix allows the user to prioritize risks for further analysis or responses. It helps to distinguish between those risks that will have a minor impact on business activities and those that will have a major impact. It usually classifies risks according to their impact probability, such as very high, high, moderate, low, and very low. The reference is the standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs, and Projects, Page# 138.

q.en: A risk manager of a new construction project. He and the team have identified a large number of risks during its risk identification. There are no time and resources for quantitative analysis of all identified risks. The team also agreed that not all of these risks would justify the effort necessary to dig deeply into them. What should the risk manager do next?

en: Perform quantitative risk analysis for all risks.
Implement the approved risk responses.
Perform qualitative risk analysis to prioritize the risks.
Develop risk responses for all the identified risks.

x.en:
Qualitative risk analysis is applied to the list of risks created or updated by the Identify Risks process to provide management with the characteristics of the risks that have the most influence (positive or negative) on achieving the objectives. Risks that are assessed as high priority, which either threaten or enhance the achievement of objectives, are highlighted in the Plan Risk Responses process. These risks may be further analyzed using quantitative risk analysis.

The reference is the standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs, and Projects, Page#34.

q.en: A project manager identifies the project risks. As a part of this activity, he wants to know the risk attitude and Industry studies of similar projects. Which of the following should the project manager review to know the risk attitude and Industry studies of similar projects?

en: Stakeholder register.
Procurement documents.
Enterprise environmental factors
Project business case.

x.en: Enterprise and environmental factors contain the risk attitude and Industry studies of similar projects. PMBOK6 Page#38,39.

q.en: A project manager for the construction of a bridge. The project lost nine working days due to the bad climate. The project manager calls for an emergency meeting and decides to apply fast-tracking to accelerate the project. What is the above response?

en: Mitigation
Transference
Exploit
Workaround

x.en: The risk is unknown and already occurred. Workarounds are responses that were not initially planned but are required to deal with emerging risks that were previously unidentified or accepted passively.

q.en: A project manager is spending a lot of time resolving problems that happen during project execution. Which of the following would be BETTER for the project manager to focus on?

en: Transfer the problems to other projects.
Ask the team to solve the problems.
Execute the project management plan.
Identify additional risks and follow the risk management process.

x.en: The project manager should be proactive, conduct a risk management process and identify the risks. He should not wait until the problems happen and then resolve them. The cost of risk management is less than the cost of solving the problems.

q.en: You are a project manager in your organization, you identified all knowable risks that may impact the project, assessed, prioritized and response plans are assigned to the risks. While you are in the execution stage of the project, one of the identified risks occurs. How will you deal with the risk?

en: Workaround
Expert judgment
Fallback plan
Management reserve

x.en: The identified risks are handled by a fallback plan if occur.

q.en: A project manager is working on planning risk responses. However, one particular risk with a negative impact cannot be avoided or mitigated. Furthermore, there is no way to transfer risk by outsourcing or buying insurance. What is the best the project manager can do about the risk?

en: Acceptance
Exploit the risk by adding state of the art resources.
Add the secondary risk to the register.
Update the Risk Response.

q.en: A project manager has identified a risk in the project that is difficult for him to manage. The project manager gives the responsibility to manage this risk to outsourcing. What is the selected risk response strategy?

en: Transfer
Mitigate
Avoid
Exploit

x.en:
The transfer involves shifting the responsibility of a threat to a third party to manage the risk and bear the impact of the threat occurs. Risk transfer often involves payment of a risk premium to the party taking on the threat.

The reference is the standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs, and Projects, Page#36.

q.en: You work as a project manager for MEGA Inc. You are preparing to plan risk responses for your project with your project team. What are the risk responses for a negative risk event in the project?

en: Escalate, Avoid, Mitigate, Transfer and Accept.
Escalate, Avoid, Mitigate, Accept and Exploit.
Escalate, Avoid, Mitigate, Share and Accept.
Escalate, Avoid, Mitigate, Enhance and Accept.

x.en:
Risk response plans for negative risks are Escalate, Avoid, Mitigate, Transfer and Accept. 

The reference is the standard for risk management in portfolios, programs, and projects page#36

q.en: In your project site the generator always outages, therefore you bought a backup generator, what is the risk response strategy?

en: Avoidance
Acceptance
Enhance
Mitigation

x.en:
In risk mitigation, action is taken to reduce the probability of occurrence and/or impact of a threat. An early mitigation action is often more effective than trying to repair the damage after the threat has occurred. Where it is not possible to reduce the probability, a mitigation response might reduce the impact by targeting factors that drive the severity. 

The reference is the standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs, and Projects, Page#36.

q.en: You are a project manager at Delta Inc. The Sponsor informed you that no way to delay the schedule but he doesn’t care about cost or quality .what is the risk tolerance of the sponsor?

en: High-risk tolerance in the schedule but high-risk tolerance in cost and quality.
Low-risk tolerance in the schedule but low-risk tolerance in cost and quality.
Low-risk tolerance in schedule, cost, and quality.
Low-risk tolerance in the schedule but high-risk tolerance in cost and quality.

x.en: The sponsor has low-risk tolerance in schedule, due to the degree, amount, or volume of risk that the sponsor will Withstand is low, and has high-risk tolerance in the cost or quality because he does not care so the volume of risk in cost and quality that the sponsor will Withstand is high.

q.en: You are a project manager identifying the project stakeholders. Which of the following is an example of stakeholder identification methods?

en: Risk probability and impact matrix.
Perform Quantitative analysis.
Plan stakeholder qualitative analysis.
Stakeholders’ analysis.

x.en: Stakeholder analysis results in a list of stakeholders and relevant information such as their positions in the organization, roles on the project, “stakes,” expectations, attitudes (their levels of support for the project), and their interest in information about the project. PMBOK5 Page# 512

q.en: Which one of the following is the best description of the risk averse stakeholder?

en: Tend to be adaptable and resourceful, enjoying life and not afraid to take action or even thrill seeking. This can lead to a somewhat casual approach towards threats, as welcomes the challenge of tackling the uncertainty head-on.

Implies being reasonably comfortable with most uncertainty, accepting that it exists as a normal feature of everyday life, including projects and business. Trends to take uncertainty in their stride, with no apparent or significant influence on their behavior. And may appear balanced.
Uncomfortable with uncertainty, has a low tolerance for ambiguity and seeks security and resolution in the face of risk.

Sees present risk-taking as a price worth paying for future pay-offs, seeks strategies and tactics that have high future pay-offs. They think abstractly and creatively and envisage possibilities, enjoying ideas and not being afraid of change or the unknown. For both threats and opportunities. He is quite mature, focusing on the longer-term and only taking action when it is likely to lead to significant benefit.

x.en:
Risk averse or adverse is a person or group who feels uncomfortable with uncertainty, has a low tolerance for ambiguity, and seeks security and resolution in the face of risk.

Risk Tolerant implies being reasonably comfortable with most uncertainty, accepting that it exists as a normal feature of everyday life, including projects and business. The risk-tolerant person or group tends to take uncertainty in their stride, with no apparent or significant influence on their behaviour. Risk-tolerance may appear balanced, but progress cannot be made while remaining perfectly balanced.

Risk Neutral sees present risk-taking as a price worth paying for future pay-offs. Risk-neutral individuals and groups are neither risk-averse nor risk-seeking, but rather seek strategies and tactics that have high future pay-offs. They think abstractly and creatively and envisage possibilities, enjoying ideas and not being afraid of change or the unknown. For both threats and opportunities, this risk-neutral approach is quite mature, focusing on the longer-term and only taking action when it is likely to lead to significant benefit.

Risk Seeker tend to be adaptable and resourceful, enjoying life and not afraid to take action or even thrill seeking. This can lead to a somewhat casual approach towards threats, as the risk-seeker welcomes the challenge of tackling the uncertainty head-on.

q.en: You are a project manager of a complex project. You have just completed the plan risk management process. Which one of the following options contains items from the risk management plan?

en: Stakeholders' risk tolerance, risk management methodology, risk management organization, and thresholds and corresponding definitions.
Project scope statement, risk management organization, templates, and milestone plan.
Stakeholders' risk tolerance, risk management methodology, scope statement, thresholds and corresponding definitions.
Risk templates, Risk management organization, risk communication plan, and milestone plan.

x.en:
The scope statement is in the scope baseline not in the risk management plan. Milestones list in the project documents and the project schedule not in the risk management plan.

The risk management plan contains the following:-

• Introduction;• Project description;• Risk management methodology;• Risk management organization;• Roles, responsibilities, and authority;• Stakeholder risk tolerance;• Criteria for success;• Risk management tools and guidelines for use;• Thresholds and corresponding definitions;• Templates;• Communications plan;• Strategy;• Risk breakdown structure. Budgeting. Timing. Definitions. Reporting formats. Tracking. Risk management scope and objectives. Use of tools.

q.en: A risk manager for a construction project. He and the project team members successfully identified and analyzed risks. Now they are working on the plan risk responses process, as a part of this process, what is the objective of mitigating negative risks?

en: Increase the probability of a risk occurrence and increase the impact.
Increase the probability of a risk occurrence and reduce the impact.
Change the probability of a risk occurrence and reduce the impact.
Reduce the probability of risk occurrence and reduce the impact.

x.en:
In risk mitigation, action is taken to reduce the probability of occurrence and/or impact of a threat. An early mitigation action is often more effective than trying to repair the damage after the threat has occurred. Where it is not possible to reduce the probability, a mitigation response might reduce the impact by targeting factors that drive the severity.

The reference is the standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs, and Projects, Page#36.

en: Share
Avoid
Accept
Mitigate

x.en:
Risk acceptance acknowledges the existence of a threat, but no proactive action is taken. This strategy may be appropriate for low-priority threats, and it may also be used where it is not possible or cost effective to address a threat in any other way. Acceptance can be either active or passive. The most common active acceptance strategy is to establish a contingency reserve, including amounts of time, money, or other resources to handle the threat if it occurs. Passive acceptance involves no proactive action apart from a periodic review of the threat to ensure that it does not change significantly. 

The reference is the standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs, and Projects, Page# 36.

q.en: A project manager of a paratheatrical project has determined that an activity is complex to complete internally, so he hires a licensed contractor to complete the work. Within the above context, what is the project manager doing?

en: Risk avoidance.
Risk transfer.
Risk exploit.
Risk mitigation.

x.en: Risk transfer involves shifting the responsibility of a threat to a third party to manage the risk and bear the impact of the threat occurs. Risk transfer often involves payment of a risk premium to the party taking on the threat. The reference is the standard for risk management in portfolios, programs, and projects page# 36.

q.en: You are a project manager of a new project. During the planning phase of your project, you learn that the sponsor has eliminated some important deliverables in other projects over the past two years, producing a negative schedule variance. What should you do next?

en: Update the issue in the issue log.
Add the risk to the risk register.
Update the lessons learned.
update the scope baseline.

x.en: You have to add this risk in the register to create responses to avoid or mitigate the variance if the sponsor eliminates any deliverable.

q.en: You are a project manager of an airport project for your organization PESTL Inc. During the review meeting with the CEO and executive managers, one of the executives scrutinizes the project risks, including risks on the watch list. Then he requests you to create actions to close out the risks on the watch list. What is the risk attitude of this executive manager?

en: Risk Appetite.
Risk Seeker.
Risk Tolerant.
Risk Averse.

x.en: Risk Averse is a person or group that feels uncomfortable with uncertainty, has a low tolerance for ambiguity, and seeks security and resolution in the face of risk.

q.en: You are assigned as a project manager to a new construction project. The project sponsor has requested you ensure that the project risks are closely managed. You start with developing the risk management plan. Within the above context, what is the expected outcome of developing the risk management plan?

en: Defining how risk management will be executed throughout the project.
Define the communication strategy for risks throughout the project.
The ability to identify risks throughout the project lifecycle.
Monitor and control risks throughout the project lifecycle.

x.en:
The objectives of the Plan Risk Management process are to: develop the overall risk management strategy, decide how the risk management processes will be executed, and integrate risk management with all other activities.

Effective risk management requires the creation of a risk management plan. This plan describes how the risk management processes are to be carried out and how they fit in with other processes. The reference is the standard for risk management in portfolios, programs, and projects page# 30.

q.en: When should the project manager close the project risks?

en: When the risks have been realized and can no longer happen again.
When the forecast date has been met or exceeded.
When the high management agrees that risks are no longer applicable.
When the analysis determines the risks are not applicable.

x.en:
The most commonly adopted terms to describe the status of risk are:

■ Active. The risk is still alive and relevant to the organizational activity

■ Closed. Either the risk can no longer happen or have an impact on the activity, or it has materialized and has been transferred onto the issue log for action.

It is good practice to document the reasons for closure in the risk register, for example:

●● Risk impacted, managed as an issue

●● Risk did not occur

●● Risk successfully managed.

q.en: The following table is given. Based on this table, which of the following risks has the highest exposure?

en: Risk3
Risk4
Risk1
Risk2

x.en: According to the risk probability and impact matrix, Risk1 is the highest risk exposure. (M x VH)

q.en: A project manager of a new project that is just starting. The company has a low-risk tolerance and appetite for the project due to budget and schedule constraints. The project stakeholders are very involved in the project and want to ensure that there is clear visibility of the project risks and progress. Within the above context, how should the project manager handle the stakeholders’ expectations?

en: Establish contingency reserve for the schedule to accommodate risks.
Share the risk response strategies with the stakeholders.
Ensure the risk register contains all the identified project risks.
Create a communication plan to share updates on risks.

x.en: Escalating risk-related information to management and other stakeholders reflects the stakeholder’s risk appetite and expectations. As the work evolves, maintaining effective communications with the stakeholders enables portfolio, program, and project managers to become aware of any changes in the stakeholders’ attitudes and adapt the risk management approach to take into account any new factors. The reference is the standard for risk management in portfolios, programs, and projects page# 30.

q.en: A project manager of a construction project. He has been informed that the concrete is unable to be used because heavy rain affected its consistency This possibility and its estimated costs were already identified in the risk register. How should he fund the additional costs?

en: Use the contingency reserve
Use the procurement budget
Use the management reserve
Use the budget reserve

x.en: The risk has already been identified in the risk register, so you have to use the contingency reserve that is allocated for identified risks. Contingency reserves are often viewed as part of the budget intended to address the known unknowns that can affect a project.

q.en: A project manager for constructing a bridge over the river. The team is in its first month of construction. The subject matter experts report that there is a possibility of the climate being heavier this year and informs that the earlier designs may have to be redesigned considering the additional water pressure expected. What is the best immediate action the project manager should do?

en: Issue a change request and submit it to CCB for approval.
Redesign the project immediately to mitigate the impact.
meet with all stakeholders to discuss this risk.
Update the Risk register to add this risk with its probability and impact.

x.en: The best immediate action is “Add the risk to the Risk register” to manage this risk according to the risk management best practice. The possible impact and risk probability should also be added. No other action should be performed prior to adding the risk to the register.

q.en: A project manager of a new project. During the risk audit, it was found that some risks were not analyzed correctly because risk-related information was not properly reviewed before concluding characteristics of risks like probability, impact and priority. What should have been done to prevent this problem?

en: Analysis of all risk characteristics early in the project.
Risk data quality assessment.
Escalate to the sponsor.
Accurate Risk probability and impact assessment.

x.en:
The results of the risk analysis are only as good as the data collected. A review of the reliability and sufficiency of the data ensures that the analysis is based on high-quality information. Data that are deemed to be of lesser quality may be further researched or excluded from the risk analysis. Care should be taken when excluding poor quality data to avoid a less-than-robust qualitative analysis. The reference is the standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs, and Projects, Page# 139.

Risk data quality assessment evaluates the degree to which the data about individual project risks is accurate and reliable as a basis for qualitative risk analysis. The use of low-quality risk data may lead to a qualitative risk analysis that is of little use to the project. If data quality is unacceptable, it may be necessary to gather better data. Risk data quality may be assessed via a questionnaire measuring the project’s stakeholder perceptions of various characteristics, which may include completeness, objectivity, relevancy, and timeliness. A weighted average of selected data quality characteristics can then be generated to give an overall quality score. PMBOK6 page# 423.

q.en: You are a risk manager of an airport project. You notice that a risk owner is facing challenges during the implementation of a response strategy and the costs are significantly exceeding expectations. What should you do first?

en: Perform a cost-benefit analysis.
Modify the risk response strategy.
Analyze the situation and meet with the risk owner.
Escalate the situation to the project manager.

x.en: The first step, you should study and analyze the situation then meet the risk owner to know what should you do next.

q.en: The sponsor of a critical project has scheduled a meeting with the risk team leader to determine more information on managing threats and opportunities. What are two actions the project risk team leader should do to evaluate the project environment and the chances of managing them? (Select two).

en: Check the contract and determine the resources and project funding.
Check the scope of work to determine the project methodology.
Schedule a meeting with the project team to know the next steps.
Examine corporate templates to check that they are considered external and internal factors.
Review the policies and practices that are available in the risk management plan.

x.en:
To evaluate the project environment and the chances of managing them


	Schedule a meeting with the project team to know the next steps.
	 
	And review the policies and practices that are available in the risk management plan.

q.en: You are a project manager in your organization, you identified all knowable risks that may impact the project, assessed, prioritized and response plans are assigned to the risks. While you are in the execution stage of the project, one unidentified risk occurs. How will you fund this risk?

en: Fallback plan.
Expert judgment.
Contingency reserve.
Management Reserve.

x.en: The Unidentified risks are funded by management reserve and handled by workaround if occur. Management reserves are intended to address the “unknown unknowns” that can affect a project. The management reserve is not included in the cost baseline but is part of the overall project budget and funding requirements. When an amount of management reserves is used to fund unforeseen work, the amount of management reserve used is added to the cost baseline, thus requiring an approved change to the cost baseline.

q.en: Which of the following should be used to determine how often a risk register of a project should be updated or reviewed in a given year when the project is in a very high business rhythm?

en: The risk response plan.
The risk management plan.
The risk exposure process.
The portfolio management plan

x.en:
The risk management plan defines both the normal frequency for repeating the processes in addition to specific or exceptional conditions under which the corresponding actions are initiated. 

The reference is the standard for risk management in portfolios, programs, and projects page#30.

q.en: You are a risk manager of a construction project. Now you are facilitating risk planning activities with the project team. The team is documenting all the checkpoints and the way that might indicate delays on critical deliverables. The above is an example of

en: Risk triggers.
Issue log.
Risk register.
Risk strategy.

x.en:
Trigger Condition. An event or situation that indicates that a risk is about to occur. Triggers may be discovered during the risk identification process and monitored during the project execution. Once the risk trigger occurs, the project team needs to implement risk responses. PMBOK6 page#725.

Trigger Condition: Events that trigger the contingency response, such as missing intermediate milestones or gaining higher priority with a supplier, should be defined and tracked.

q.en: During the status meeting, one of the department managers complains that the backup power supply failed and impacted the system in the department negatively. The project manager reviews the risk register and has discovered that the risk was known and accepted. After reviewing the minutes of the meeting, it was determined that the department manager was not in the planning phase of risk management. Which identification method should have been performed?

en: Control risk process.
Stakeholder analysis.
Monte Carlo.
Qualitative analysis.

x.en: Only stakeholder analysis is an identification tool/technique. Stakeholder analysis is a technique of systematically gathering and analyzing quantitative and qualitative information to determine whose interests should be taken into account throughout the project. It identifies the interests, expectations, and influence of the stakeholders and relates them to the purpose of the project. It also helps to identify stakeholder relationships.

q.en: Kelly is a project manager of a project for the development of the interface systems between the railway stations to handle the tickets around the country. Kelly with the risk manager and the project team agreed on the contingency reserve for the identified risks mitigation. While the project was in the execution stage, one of the team members discovers a residual risk that wasn’t identified during the plan risk responses process. This risk may impact the schedule. Within the above context, what should Kelly do to handle this risk?

en: Analyze the risk and update the risk register.
Ignore the risk.
Ask the sponsor.
Accept the risk, since it’s a residual risk.

x.en: Identification and analyzing risk processes are iterative, she has to identify and analyze any new risk that arises during the project life cycle and update the register. The Residual risks that remain after the responses are implemented. These residual risks are clearly identified, analyzed, documented, and communicated to all relevant stakeholders until they are satisfied. The Reference is the Standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs, and Projects, Page# 37.

q.en: You are a project manager of a new project; you and your team need to develop the risk register. When should you identify the project risks?

en: Only at the project's midpoint for the stakeholders to review them.
You should ensure that project team members proactively identify risks throughout the project to plan for possible response strategies.
You should Identify risks at the start of the project because the risk exposure will not be changed.
You should delegate the risk identification to each team member to identify and record the risks on separate risk registers for their areas.

x.en:
You should ensure that project team members proactively identify risks throughout the project to plan for possible response strategies.

Identify Risks is an iterative process, since new individual project risks may emerge as the project progresses through its life cycle and the level of overall project risk will also change. The frequency of iteration and participation in each risk identification cycle will vary by situation, and this will be defined in the risk management plan.

q.en: An industrial design firm has over 5 USD billion in the current contract. As a result of quantitative risk analysis of a multinational project, opportunities have been identified and assessed as high priorities for the project. What is the most effective method to capture these opportunities?

en: Buy insurance.
Mitigate
Accept
Assign Contingency reserve.

x.en: In some cases, you can use contingency reserve to enhance opportunity or exploit.

q.en: Your organization is very comfortable with ignoring risks, They don’t care and never pay any attention to risk until it becomes an issue. What is the attitude of your Organization?

en: Risk Seeker
Risk Tolerant
Risk Neutral
Risk Avers.

x.en: Risk Tolerant is very conformable with ignoring the risk; they don’t care and never pay any attention to risks until becoming an issue.

q.en: Eng.Tarek saeed is a project manager of the smart project; He is now in the process which is prioritizing risks for further analysis or action by assessing and combining their probability of occurrence and impact which enables him to reduce the level of uncertainty and to focus on high priority risks. What is that process?

en: Identify risk.
Plan risk management.
Qualitative risk analysis.
Quantitative risk analysis.التحليل الكمي للمخاطر.

x.en: Perform Qualitative Risk Analysis is the process of prioritizing risks for further analysis or action by assessing and combining their probability of occurrence and impact. The key benefit of this process is that it enables project managers to reduce the level of uncertainty and focus on high-priority risks.

q.en: You work as a project manager for Doca Desta Inc. You and your team calculate the contingency reserve for the project. What is the contingency reserve of your project as per the following Risk in the below table?

q.en: You are a project manager working on a long-term and high-visibility project at an organization that has a very low-risk appetite for this project due to the direct impact on the organization's business. The sponsor meets weekly with you. You were just informed by one of the risk owners that the exposure from two high-impact risks is reached the risk thresholds. What should you do next?

en: Revise and update the project management plan to add a contingency reserve.
You should complete an assessment and confirm the response with the sponsors.
Conduct mitigation measurements for those risks.
Conduct an assumptions and constraints analysis.

x.en: The organization has a very low-risk appetite for this project due to its direct impact on the company's business. Therefore, you should perform risk reassessment, including risk identification, analysis, and response planning, that is repeated at reasonable intervals, or in response to project events—without generating excessive administrative overhead. So, you should complete the assessment and then confirm the response with the sponsor.

q.en: You are a project manager of the construction project. Which project reserves should you use to budget for known risks?

en: Cost reserve
Budget reserve
Contingency Reserve.
Management reserve.

x.en: The strategies developed to deal with risks at the project level consist of activities guided by the risk management plan, budgeted accordingly, and funded by the project’s contingency reserve. The reference is the standard for risk management in portfolios, programs, and projects page#59.

q.en: A critical project that had 300 risks is almost done. The project manager is closing the risks as part of the closing process. One of the project team members mentions that there are important documents to be updated. Which one of the following documents will need to be updated?

en: Program register.
Stakeholder register
Lessons learned.
Risk register.

x.en: At project closure, the project manager should ensure that a description has been given of the closure of every risk in the risk register, for example: (a) did not occur; (b) occurred and contingency plan invoked, or (c) occurred and impact to the project scope (i.e., time, cost, and quality).

q.en: You are a project manager working on a project for which some requirements are not clearly defined. The client insists that this should not be considered a problem and the project should continue without delay. Within the above context, what should you do?

en: Discuss the concerns with the team during the meeting.
Log the risk in the risk register.
Negotiate the matter with the client to avoid the risk.
Accept the risk.

x.en: If requirements are not clearly defined, that means a risk and the first step is, you should Log the risk in the risk register then analyze the risk and assign appropriate risk responses.

q.en: You are a risk manager determining the stakeholders’ risk attitude. Which of the following represents levels of risk attitudes?

en: Political, Internal, External.
Risk averse, risk avoiding, risk matrix.
Risk averse, risk neutral, risk seeking.
Very low, medium, very high.

x.en: Risk attitude is a disposition toward uncertainty, adopted explicitly or implicitly by individuals and groups, driven by perception, and evidenced by observable behaviour. Risk attitude represents an organization’s approach to assessing and eventually pursuing, retaining, taking, or turning away from risk. Risk attitudes can range from risk averse to risk seeking. The Reference is the Standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs, and Projects, Page#8

q.en: You have just been assigned as the project manager of an upgrade of a pipeline project. During the planning meeting, the project team decides to conduct a site survey to define the ground conditions before the engineering stage. Within the above context, which of the following risk management processes is the team implementing?

en: Perform Quantitative Risk Analysis Process.
Plan Risk Management Process.
Plan Risk Responses Process.
Identify Risks Process.

x.en: The team is performing the Identify risks process to identify the knowable risks that may impact the project objectives before the engineering stage.

q.en: Which one of the following options is the most accurate definition of project risk?

en: An uncertain event can affect at least one project objective.
An unknown event can affect the project schedule.
Uncertain event or condition within the project.
An uncertain event can affect the project costs.

x.en:
A risk is an uncertain event or condition that, if it occurs, has a positive or negative effect on one or more objectives.

The Reference is the Standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs, and Projects Page#7.

q.en: You are a risk manager of a new project. You want to use a technique to justify risk response decisions taken on a high-risk project. What is this technique?

en: Brainstorming
Probability and impact matrix.
Nominal group technique.
Decision tree analysis.

x.en:
Decision tree analysis causes the organization to structure the costs and benefits of decisions when the results are determined in part by uncertainty and risk.

The solution of the decision tree helps select the decision that provides the highest expected monetary value or expected utility to the organization. The reference is the standard for risk management in portfolios, programs, and projects page#152.

q.en: You are a risk manager of a new project. You have completed the risk management plan. Now you are identifying all knowable risks. The sponsor believes that the important risks are the financial risks and no need for additional risk management. Within the above context, what method should you use to identify risks from other potential topics such as quality, technical, internal, external, performance and project management?

en: Perform root cause analysis and create an Ishikawa diagram.
Use probability and impact matrix.
Use prompt lists and risk breakdown structure.
Review the functional units in the organization.

x.en:
The risk breakdown structure (RBS) is a hierarchical framework of potential sources of risk to a project (Technical, management, internal, external, commercial.). Offers a framework for other risk identification techniques such as brainstorming

• Ensures coverage of all types of risk

• Tests for blind spots or omissions.

Prompt lists enumerate risk categories with the purpose of detecting the most relevant to the project, program, or portfolio. Offers a framework for other risk identification techniques

such as brainstorming and interviews.

Categories of risks include Technical risks, Organizational risks, and External risks.

· Ensures coverage of all types of risk

· Stimulates creativity.

The Reference is the Standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs, and Projects, Page#148, 133,154,155.

q.en: Which of the following tools can the project risk manager use to help identify and assess project risks?

en: Reserve analysis.
Stakeholder analysis.
Interviews
Risk survey

x.en:
Interviews can be used in identify the risk process and perform qualitative risk analysis.

Interviewing experienced project participants, stakeholders, and subject matter experts helps to identify risks.
The level of probability for each risk and its impact on each objective is evaluated during the interview or meeting. Explanatory detail, including assumptions justifying the levels assigned.

q.en: You are a project manager of a construction project for your organization. The Sponsor wants to reduce the cost of the risk management activities. What did you fail to do?

en: Communicating the risk management activities and their benefits.
Creating a risk management plan.
Discussing the importance of the contingency reserve.
Exploiting all the opportunities.

x.en:
Honest and open communication is a key success factor in risk management.

Effective Project Risk Management benefits from robust communication and consultation with stakeholders. This enables agreement among stakeholders that Project Risk Management in general.

Everyone is involved in the risk management process. Any actions or attitudes that hinder communication about risk reduce the effectiveness of risk management regarding proactive approaches and effective decision making.

Risk standard page# 17.

q.en: You are a project manager of a construction project. You performed a variance analysis on the project during the execution phase. The variances are increasing. What does this result mean or imply?

en: No future deviation.
The uncertainty and risk are increasing.
Your project is over budget.
Your project is behind schedule.

x.en: The analysis of variances compares planned versus actual results. When the variances are increasing, there is increased uncertainty and risk. Outcomes from this analysis may forecast any potential for future deviation from the baseline plan prior to completion. Deviation from the baseline plan may indicate the potential impact of threats or opportunities. The reference is the standard for risk management in portfolios, programs, and projects page# 149.

q.en:
You are a risk manager of a construction project. Now you and the project team are brainstorming about risk management. You want all the project team members to join the risk prioritization session for the identified risks. The project manager refuses the participation of all project team members because of some resources consideration.

Within the above context, what should you do?

en: Convince the project manager about the importance of the participation of all project team members in all risk management process.
Escalate that to the sponsor.
Don't care about the project manager's decision and allow all the project team to participate then explain to the project manager the benefit of that.
Agree with the project manager and start prioritization by a few numbers of team members.

x.en:
Convince the project manager about the importance of the project team members in all risk management process.

Everyone should be involved in the Project Risk Management process "risk management is everyone’s responsibility". It's a key success factor of risk management. The reference is the standard for risk management in portfolios, programs, and projects page#17.

q.en: The feasibility of the risk management planning is dependent upon .......

en: Agreed upon definitions.
Manageability and maturity.
Culture, people, and infrastructure capabilities.
Alignment with the PMO and the PMIS.

x.en: One of the critical success factors of plan risk management is: Comply with the Organization’s Objectives, Policies, and Practices. The feasibility of risk management planning is dependent upon the features of the organization in which it is carried out. The rules and guidelines defined in the risk management plan should be compatible with the culture of the organization, its capabilities from the point of view of people and facilities, and its values, goals, and objectives. The Standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs, and Projects, Page# 30.

q.en: A project manager of a new stadium project identified a risk of communication issues with the client which may impact the project schedule. The sales team leader advises that this client prefers face-to-face discussions. What should the project manager do to avoid this risk?

en: He should record the risk and the client's preference in the risk register.
Send an email, call the client and advise that online communication is faster.
Request the sales leader to lead the communication with the client.
He should meet the client and plan for milestone meetings.

x.en:
The first step: He should record the risk and the client's preference in the risk register. The advice of the sales leader is the preliminary response. The second step: meet the client.

When a risk is first identified, preliminary responses may be identified at the same time. These are recorded during the Identify Risks process and are considered for immediate action when such action is appropriate. When such responses are not implemented immediately, they should be considered during the Plan Risk Responses process.

The reference is the standard for risk management in portfolios, programs, and projects page# 32.

q.en: You are a project manager of a new project. you and the project team have identified a risk event in the project with a very high probability of occurrence and the risk event has a high-cost impact on the project. You discuss the risk event with the customer. The customer decides that the requirements surrounding the risk event should be removed from the project. The removal of the requirements does affect the project scope, but it can release the project from high-risk exposure. What is the above risk response?

en: Exploit
Avoidance
Passive acceptance.
Mitigation

x.en:
The response is risk avoidance by removing the requirements.

Risk avoidance is when the portfolio, program, or project team acts to eliminate a threat or protect activity from risk impact. It may be appropriate for a high-priority threat with a high probability of occurrence and a large negative impact. Avoidance may involve changing some aspect of the management plan or changing the objective that is in jeopardy in order to eliminate the threat impact entirely. Should the risk materialize, it would have no effect with respect to the objective. The risk owner may also take action to isolate the objective from the risk’s impact if it were to occur. 

 

The reference is the Standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs, and Projects, page# 36.

q.en: Risk management is essential for all projects and adds value to all processes. Risk management is a critical success factor for the projects. Which of the following are considered supportive elements for effective risk management?

en: Competent people, functional organization, procedures, policy, and tools and techniques.
Supportive organization, competent people, simple scalable process, and tools and techniques.
Trained people, balanced matrix organization, simple scalable process, and tools and techniques.
Competent people, Directive organization, rigorous process, and tools and techniques.

x.en:
The risk management plan includes the tailored risk management processes, which are based on the process maturity of the organization. Scalable elements of the process that are a part of risk management planning include, but are not limited to:

Available resources,

Escalation paths,

Methodology and processes used,

Tools and techniques used,

Supporting infrastructure,

Review and update frequency,

Reporting requirements.

The reference is the standard for risk management in portfolios, programs, and projects page#31.

q.en: You are a project manager for a big project. You want to integrate the risk information into the project management plan. So you want to send the data to the estimators and the analysts on regular basis. How often should you send the information to the analysts and estimators?

en: Should be monthly.
As per the organization's policy.
As per the risk management plan.
Should be Weekly.

x.en:
The timing and budgeting are in the risk management plan.

Timing: Defines when and how often the risk management processes will be performed throughout the project life cycle, establishes protocols for application of schedule contingency reserves, and establishes risk management activities for inclusion in the project schedule. 

The risk management plan defines the normal frequency for repeating the processes. The Reference is the Standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs, and Projects, Page#30.

q.en:
You are the project manager of a new project. While you are in the execution stage, the project team realizes that the power supply outlet for the purchased equipment is not compatible with the existing electrical infrastructure in the project area. This risk was not identified. You decided to buy a new power adapter.

What is the best description for your action?

en: Workaround
Management reserve.
Contingent plan.
Fallback plan.

x.en: The risk was unknown during the planning and occurs during execution. You purchased an adapter of the risk occurrence, so it is a workaround.

q.en: You work as a project manager for Organization. You are preparing to plan risk responses for your project with your project team. What are the risk responses for a positive risk event in the project?

en: Escalate, Exploit, Enhance, Accept and Share.
Escalate, Exploit, Enhance, Accept and Transfer.
Escalate, Exploit, Mitigate, Enhance and Accept.
Escalate, Exploit, Enhance, Share and Avoid.

x.en: Risk response plans for positive risks are escalate, exploit, enhance, share, and accept. The reference is the standard for risk management in portfolios, programs, and projects pages #36&37.

q.en: You are a risk manager for the construction of a hospital project. You notice that one of the project risks is likely to cause a negative impact of 15000 USD with a probability of 50%. At the same time, there is a possibility of saving 10000 USD by using alternative resources, this has a likelihood of 25%. What is the EMV of your project?
